paragraphs: Two survey crews arrived at the same abandoned conservatory with orders bearing the same seal. Each had been promised exclusive access to the glasshouse at its center. By the time {{heroPlayer}}’s team saw {{otherPlayer}}’s lamps through the vines, both crews had already planted their boundary flags.

{{hero}} found the conservatory’s old irrigation controls beneath a bed of dead orchids. Opening the valves revealed a second boundary, drawn decades earlier in blue ceramic beneath the soil. A burst pipe sent water through the trenches, washing the newer flags away while the two crews argued across the glass.

The original marker lay under a fallen tree that neither crew could move alone. {{hero}} worked the buried valve until water loosened the roots, then reached beneath them for the ceramic seal. A shout came from the opposite door. For one breath, both crews were close enough to read the same inscription.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew carried out the original seal and claimed the glasshouse it marked.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew reached the seal first and kept the conservatory behind its boundary.
endings.draw: The seal broke in two, leaving each crew with a claim the other refused to recognize.

paragraphs: A bell rang each night from a chapel that had been sealed for generations. {{heroPlayer}}’s pilgrims wanted the doors opened before dawn; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail had orders to keep everyone off the hill. Neither side knew who had lit the candle visible in the upper window.

{{hero}} crossed the ruined cloister as a defender stepped from the archway at arm’s length. Steel struck stone in the cramped passage. The fighter drove the opponent back from the chapel steps, but the bell rang again, close enough now to make the loose glass tremble in its frames.

The upper door opened on its own. Behind it stood a small figure trying to pull the bell rope down with both hands. {{hero}} lowered the weapon and held the archway while the pilgrims climbed toward the child. The security lamps swept the steps before anyone reached the top.

endings.heroWins: The pilgrims brought the child down, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the chapel open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail closed the hill again, with the bell still sounding behind the door.
endings.draw: Both sides guided the child away; neither would leave the chapel in the other’s hands.

paragraphs: The colonial land office had mapped a dry ridge through the marsh. On arrival, {{heroPlayer}}’s settlers found their future town under knee-deep water. {{otherPlayer}}’s survey detail had staked the only high ground beside a weather station whose warning light had stopped flashing the previous night.

{{hero}} waded out to the station with a coil of field cable above the water. Its instruments showed that the flood would climb again at dusk, and the settlement markers stood directly in its path. The specialist carried the cable toward a raised relay while voices called from the occupied ridge.

A floating section of boardwalk struck the relay supports. {{hero}} caught the cable before it disappeared under the planks and climbed the swaying ladder with the weather log clenched between their teeth. From that height the evacuation route was clear, though reaching the transmitter meant remaining in plain view.

endings.heroWins: The warning reached the settlers, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people held the ridge as the water rose.
endings.heroLoses: The warning arrived too late; {{otherPlayer}}’s detail kept the ridge while the settlers retreated.
endings.draw: The settlers escaped the flood, but both parties abandoned their stakes beneath the water.

paragraphs: A civic archive was scheduled to become a private vault at midnight. {{heroPlayer}}’s detail had to keep the public entrance open until its records could be copied; {{otherPlayer}}’s contractors arrived with new locks and a deed. Inside, the final clerk was still wheeling crates toward the loading lift.

{{hero}} took a position above the service hall and fired into the shutter mechanism as the contractors began closing it. The damaged shutter stopped halfway, leaving a narrow path for the clerk’s cart. Every muzzle flash from the opposite balcony reflected in the polished floor below.

The cart jammed under the shutter. The clerk tried to pull it free, but the last crate fell open and photographs scattered across the hall. {{hero}} kept the balcony covered while the clerk gathered what they could. A hand reached for the emergency release on the far wall.

endings.heroWins: The clerk escaped with the photographs, and {{heroPlayer}}’s detail held the archive entrance.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s contractors sealed the hall around the abandoned crates.
endings.draw: The clerk saved some records; the shutter remained stuck between two competing claims.

paragraphs: A hillside seed vault held the last viable crop from a burned valley. {{heroPlayer}}’s relief party came to move its samples before the fire crossed the road. {{otherPlayer}}’s guards had secured the vault for another shipment, and the smoke was already hiding the lower terraces.

{{hero}} reached the vault’s cooling controls through a side vent too narrow for a carrier. The temperature rose with each passing minute; opening the main door would ruin the seeds before the boxes could be packed. The specialist found a manual bypass that fed cold air into the loading passage.

The bypass wheel seized with the passage half cooled. Outside, the first trees caught and a guard called for everyone to clear the hillside. {{hero}} braced a foot against the wall and turned the wheel another fraction, making room for one crate at a time while smoke rolled through the vent.

endings.heroWins: The last crate crossed the road with {{heroPlayer}}’s relief party before the fire reached the vault.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards kept the vault and its surviving seed stock behind their cordon.
endings.draw: Both parties saved crates, but the flames left neither a vault to claim.

paragraphs: A listening post on the ice recorded a voice calling from inside the glacier. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol followed it to a weather mast, where {{otherPlayer}}’s team had already set up a recovery winch. The voice repeated its message every nine minutes, always ending before it gave a location.

{{hero}} took cover behind the mast and fired across the frozen equipment yard to keep the winch from dragging its cable away. A bullet struck an abandoned microphone, and the voice came through every open channel at once. Beneath the snow, something answered the new sound with three heavy knocks.

The patrol found a seam opening across the ice between the mast and the winch. {{hero}} watched the opposing team retreat from the crack, then saw one of their crew slip toward it. There was time to cover a rescue or secure the recording gear, but no route that would keep both safe.

endings.heroWins: The stranded crew member reached firm ice, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol carried the recording away.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team took the recorder as the patrol withdrew from the widening seam.
endings.draw: Everyone left the equipment behind; the voice kept calling from beneath the glacier.

paragraphs: A ferry pier resurfaced each low tide after years beneath the bay. {{heroPlayer}}’s divers came for the navigation ledger sealed in its office; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol had marked the pier as a restricted salvage site. The tide chart gave both crews less than an hour before the office went under again.

{{hero}} entered through a skylight and found the ledger chained to a desk. A tide clock on the wall still worked, its brass hand moving toward the red mark. The specialist freed one end of the chain while water pressed through a door that somebody outside had opened.

The pages were too fragile to drag through the rising water. {{hero}} lifted the ledger onto the upper shelf and sent photographs through a portable link as the office filled. Above the skylight, footsteps crossed the roof. A rope dropped beside the desk, but there was no sign whose hand held it.

endings.heroWins: The photographs reached shore, and {{heroPlayer}}’s divers recovered the ledger before the tide swallowed the pier.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol controlled the pier when the water returned, with the ledger still inside.
endings.draw: Both crews escaped with partial photographs while the ledger disappeared beneath the bay.

paragraphs: An observatory had tracked a falling object to the crater behind its eastern dome. {{heroPlayer}}’s retrieval team reached the grounds at the same time as {{otherPlayer}}’s guards. Lightning kept striking the unfinished antenna above the crater, briefly showing a shape half buried in the dust.

{{hero}} climbed into the dome and fired at the supports of a mobile floodlight that was exposing the retrieval crew. The light tipped harmlessly into the gravel. In the sudden darkness, the object began transmitting a string of numbers through the observatory’s old speakers.

The numbers counted down as storm water collected in the crater. {{hero}} could see the opposing guards moving toward the object and the retrieval crew trapped beyond an electrified fence. The fighter kept the crossing covered, holding a line of fire while the antenna snapped overhead.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team reached the crater and carried the object clear of the rising water.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the object as the dome lights finally failed.
endings.draw: The antenna collapsed into the crater, leaving both teams with a recording and no object.

paragraphs: Someone had filed a demolition order for a crowded night market, then replaced the street number with one that did not exist. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came for the original permit; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail arrived to clear the block. Shopkeepers kept trading while the crews argued over whose map was current.

{{hero}} traced the order to a public terminal beneath a fabric stall. Its last login belonged to a vendor who had died five years earlier. The specialist copied the access record as a second authorization appeared on the screen, this one instructing the terminal to erase itself.

The stall owner folded the fabric away, revealing an old street marker under the counter. {{hero}} held the marker beside the permit and found the missing number stamped on its back. Outside, engines started at the end of the lane. The record would matter only if someone could carry it past the cordon.

endings.heroWins: The investigators saved the record, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the market standing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail cleared the block before the permit could be challenged.
endings.draw: The market closed for the night; both parties left with copies of the disputed order.

paragraphs: A tidal generator fed power to two settlements, one on either side of a seawall. {{heroPlayer}}’s repair column needed access to its central control room; {{otherPlayer}}’s detail held the door under an emergency claim. With the water rising, neither settlement could afford a shutdown.

{{hero}} fired across the turbine gallery when figures moved to cut the repair column off. The fighter used the steady rhythm of the machinery to time each advance, stopping a rush at the access ladder without hitting the brittle gauges behind it. Then the turbines fell silent in the middle of a cycle.

A maintenance worker appeared behind the control-room glass, knocking on a pressure gauge that had climbed into the red. {{hero}} stepped into the open to cover the worker’s path to a manual release. The first surge struck the seawall as the worker reached for the handle.

endings.heroWins: The release held, and {{heroPlayer}}’s column restored power from the central room.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail kept the controls while the repair column withdrew above the flood line.
endings.draw: Both settlements got power back, but the damaged room stayed under a shared watch.

paragraphs: A mountain courier tower had been built on a pass that moved with every thaw. {{heroPlayer}}’s guides found its signal lamp still burning, though the path below had broken away. {{otherPlayer}}’s expedition camped on the opposite slope, waiting for a dispatch that nobody had been able to deliver.

{{hero}} crossed a narrow snow bridge with a message tube tied to a climbing line. Inside the tower, the signal mechanism had wound its chain around a packet of undelivered letters. The specialist freed the chain, but the newly lit lamp revealed fresh cracks in the bridge outside.

One letter was addressed to a household on each side of the pass. {{hero}} could take the packet back across the bridge or use the tower’s transmitter to send the warning that the pass was failing. The lamp kept turning, sweeping its light over figures gathering at both ends.

endings.heroWins: The warning went through, and {{heroPlayer}}’s guides brought the letters down the safe slope.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s expedition reached the tower while the guides turned back from the broken pass.
endings.draw: Both parties received their letters; the tower stood alone after the snow bridge fell.

paragraphs: An old battlefield lay hidden beneath a young forest. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery party came for a missing soldier’s identification tag; {{otherPlayer}}’s excavators were already marking out a construction site. The first trench exposed a row of helmets facing a direction neither map had recorded.

{{hero}} held the tree line when shots broke out near the excavation. Between bursts, a medic carried a stretcher across the marked ground. The fighter shifted fire away from the trench to give the medic a corridor, then spotted a small metal disc caught in the stretcher’s wheel.

It was the missing tag, polished by years of rain. The medic could reach the recovery party if the corridor stayed open, but an excavator’s loader was turning toward the trench. {{hero}} kept the weapon trained on its cab while the stretcher rolled over roots and old wire.

endings.heroWins: The stretcher reached {{heroPlayer}}’s people, who carried the tag and its owner’s name home.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s excavators took the ground while the recovery party left without the tag.
endings.draw: The medic saved the tag; both parties agreed to leave the helmets undisturbed.

paragraphs: A peat bridge joined two villages that no longer spoke to each other. {{heroPlayer}}’s people came to reopen it for a funeral procession; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards occupied the far bank to keep a disputed parcel of land untouched. The coffin bearers waited in the rain while both sides argued over the crossing.

{{hero}} reached the narrow bridge as a guard moved in to bar the way. There was no room to circle. The fighter met the guard at arm’s length, blade against blade, and forced a passage wide enough for the first bearers to step onto the boards.

The peat gave way beneath the rear of the procession. {{hero}} caught the coffin rope and hauled it onto the remaining planks, turning away from the guard for a moment. On the far bank, the mourners began singing an old name that both villages recognized.

endings.heroWins: The procession crossed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the bridge open for the mourners.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards closed the crossing, sending the mourners back through the rain.
endings.draw: The coffin passed between the villages; neither side claimed the damaged bridge afterward.

paragraphs: The last train into the border station arrived with every passenger gone and the luggage still aboard. {{heroPlayer}}’s search party took the platform while {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators approached from the freight yard. A conductor’s cap hung on the signal lever, though no one remembered seeing a conductor.

{{hero}} watched the empty carriages from a signal box. When a figure stepped between two cars and raised a weapon, the fighter fired through the window frame, driving the figure back toward the yard. The train lurched forward on its own, dragging a baggage cart into the platform edge.

A faint knock came from inside the cart. {{hero}} could keep the yard covered or break the box’s glass to stop the train at the next signal. Below, the search party ran after the cart, and the empty carriages began to pick up speed.

endings.heroWins: The train stopped, and {{heroPlayer}}’s party opened the cart before it left the station.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the platform as the search party lost the train.
endings.draw: The cart was saved, but the empty train disappeared beyond the final signal.

paragraphs: A dust survey station reported falling debris from an orbit that had been empty for decades. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvage team came to collect the fragments before night; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol marked the crater as a restricted research site. Each fragment carried the same tiny map, with a different route traced in red.

{{hero}} used the station’s scanner to fit the fragments together. The routes converged on a spot beneath the survey mast, where the ground rang hollow under a boot. The specialist found a hatch handle beneath the dust and turned it while the patrol’s lamps moved around the crater rim.

The hatch opened onto a ladder, and cold air rose from below. On its first rung hung a clean glove, sized for a child. {{hero}} called for a light and descended far enough to see a second set of maps drawn on the wall, all pointing away from the sky.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the mast and followed the wall maps into the hidden station.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the hatch while the salvage team left with its scattered fragments.
endings.draw: Both parties copied the maps; neither would descend until the other had gone.

paragraphs: Miners had found a buried freight lift under the city, still carrying fresh parcels to a floor that did not appear on any plan. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery squad followed the lift cable down. {{otherPlayer}}’s security crew waited at the bottom, guarding a crate that moved whenever the lift bell sounded.

{{hero}} covered the shaft from a maintenance ledge and fired at the lift’s counterweight when the security crew tried to send the crate up. The counterweight locked the cage halfway between floors. Through the mesh, a parcel split open and spilled hundreds of stamped keys onto the floor.

The bell rang again without anyone touching it. Keys began sliding toward the crate as the lift cage tilted. {{hero}} held the ledge under fire while the recovery squad reached through the mesh for a key; the metal floor creaked at every movement.

endings.heroWins: The recovery squad stopped the cage and brought the crate into {{heroPlayer}}’s hands.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s security crew freed the lift and sent the crate beyond the squad’s reach.
endings.draw: The cage jammed between floors, leaving both crews staring at the keys through the mesh.

paragraphs: A weather balloon came down in a cattle field and played tomorrow’s emergency bulletin through its torn speaker. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers went to warn the nearby farms; {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians fenced off the landing site. The bulletin named a storm no satellite had seen yet.

{{hero}} opened the balloon’s instrument case and found a memory spool still turning. Its forecast marked the low road as safe, but the creek beside it was already rising. The specialist copied the readings onto a handheld display while the cattle crowded the gate leading uphill.

The first gust flattened the fence before anyone settled the forecast. {{hero}} pulled open the uphill gate and waved the farmers through, keeping the spool’s fragile antenna above the herd. Across the field, the technicians shouted for the equipment while thunder rolled in from a clear horizon.

endings.heroWins: The farms received the warning, and {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers kept the balloon long enough to learn why.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians took the balloon while the rangers led the farmers away.
endings.draw: The farmers reached high ground; the storm tore the balloon apart before either crew could claim it.

paragraphs: A mobile clinic stopped beside the only clean well for miles. {{heroPlayer}}’s medical team needed its water to prepare a vaccine; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards had secured the well for an arriving convoy. The patients formed a quiet line between the clinic and a locked pump house.

{{hero}} found the pump’s intake clogged with strands of dark cloth. The specialist cleared a narrow channel and drew a sample, then noticed that the water running beneath the cloth was warmer than the surface flow. Someone had built a second pipe under the pump house years earlier.

The convoy’s engines sounded beyond the dunes as the clinic’s refrigerator began to lose power. {{hero}} could seal the warm pipe and fill the clinic’s tanks, or follow it back to find what had contaminated the well. A patient offered a lantern and waited for an answer.

endings.heroWins: The clinic filled its tanks, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the well open for the patients.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the pump house as the clinic left with its limited supply.
endings.draw: The patients received clean water, but both parties left the source of the warm pipe unexplained.

paragraphs: A hospice received a ledger of names whose owners were still alive, each followed by a date two days away. {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors came to learn who sent it; {{otherPlayer}}’s protection detail had orders to remove the ledger before the residents saw it. One nurse had already found her own name.

{{hero}} inspected the ledger under a reading lamp and discovered that the ink darkened near the hospice’s old radio. Every entry held a frequency beneath the handwriting. The specialist tuned the radio to the nurse’s line and heard her voice describing a room she had never entered.

From the upper floor came a crash, followed by that same voice calling for help. {{hero}} closed the ledger and climbed the stairs with the radio hissing at each step. The protection detail reached the hall at the same time, and the nurse stood between them beside an open window.

endings.heroWins: The nurse stayed safe, and {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors carried the ledger away for answers.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail removed the ledger while the visitors searched the empty upper room.
endings.draw: The nurse survived, but the ledger vanished before either party could trace its sender.

paragraphs: A harbor pilot’s beacon shone inland instead of out to sea. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock crew tried to correct it before the fog thickened; {{otherPlayer}}’s marines held the quay for a vessel due at dawn. Every few minutes a ship’s horn sounded from a part of the channel too shallow for a hull.

{{hero}} covered the beacon stairs from a net loft, firing past the lamp whenever someone moved to swing it back toward the quay. The fighter heard an answering horn beneath the loft. Through a gap in the planks, the water showed the roof of a sunken pilot boat rising with the tide.

The lamp turned once more and lit figures trapped inside the boat’s wheelhouse. {{hero}} kept the stairs covered while the dock crew lowered a line toward the roof. The incoming vessel’s horn answered from the fog, much closer than any safe chart allowed.

endings.heroWins: The crew rescued the pilot and turned the beacon seaward before {{heroPlayer}}’s vessel arrived.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s marines held the quay while the beacon kept calling ships toward shallow water.
endings.draw: The pilot escaped, but neither party could keep the beacon lit through the fog.

paragraphs: A suspended tram stopped above a ravine with its doors open and no driver aboard. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue party climbed the eastern tower while {{otherPlayer}}’s guards controlled the western terminal. Children in the tram waved a paper sign through the windows: the brakes were getting hot.

{{hero}} reached the maintenance panel beneath the eastern platform and traced a burned cable into the tram’s emergency circuit. The specialist could release the cabin toward the far terminal, where the guards waited, or draw it back against its damaged brake. A child pressed another sign against the glass: one passenger could not stand.

The cable began to smoke. {{hero}} joined two contacts with a strip of metal cut from the panel, holding them together while the motor caught. Far across the ravine a guard lowered a boarding ladder, but the cabin lurched before anyone could step onto it.

endings.heroWins: The cabin reached {{heroPlayer}}’s tower, where the rescue party carried every passenger down.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards received the tram and kept control of the terminal.
endings.draw: The passengers escaped at the western platform; both crews stayed to argue over who would repair the line.

paragraphs: An abandoned broadcast studio went live with a map of the city’s hidden shelters. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal crew entered to save the coordinates before the transmission ended; {{otherPlayer}}’s response team came to shut the studio down. On the monitor, one shelter icon blinked beneath a building scheduled for demolition.

{{hero}} patched a portable recorder into the studio console. Every time the specialist copied a coordinate, another icon vanished from the map. A voice in the headphones read the missing addresses aloud, but it belonged to the announcer whose portrait hung in the lobby, dated sixty years earlier.

The response team cut power to the upper floor. {{hero}} kept the recorder running on its own battery, writing the last address by hand as the screen faded. Somewhere below, a steel door opened and footsteps followed the studio’s old applause sign toward the darkened stairs.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew left with the full map and kept the studio transmitting long enough to warn the shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team silenced the broadcast and took possession of the remaining coordinates.
endings.draw: One address survived on paper; neither crew could account for the voice in the headphones.

paragraphs: The sculpture garden had been emptied overnight except for a row of stone faces looking toward its locked greenhouse. {{heroPlayer}}’s art handlers came to recover the missing works; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol had secured the grounds around a newly opened sinkhole. As dawn broke, each face turned a few degrees toward the hole.

{{hero}} watched the greenhouse from a broken colonnade and fired to turn back a team crossing the gravel. A ricochet struck a bronze pedestal, revealing fresh fingerprints in its dust. Inside the greenhouse, the lost sculptures stood packed in shipping frames, and a person knocked weakly from one of the crates.

The sinkhole widened beneath the colonnade. {{hero}} held the crossing clear while the handlers ran for the crate, their cutting tool sparking against its hinges. The stone faces shifted again. This time they turned toward the trapped person, and the ground under the greenhouse began to settle.

endings.heroWins: The handlers freed the prisoner and carried the works out under {{heroPlayer}}’s protection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol kept the greenhouse as the handlers abandoned their search.
endings.draw: The prisoner escaped, but the garden swallowed the sculptures before either crew could claim them.

paragraphs: A cargo tether above the station had begun lowering a sealed container without a receiving crew. {{heroPlayer}}’s dockhands wanted to catch it before it crushed the public concourse; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail sealed the winch room around the cargo manifest. The label on the container read only RETURN TO SENDER.

{{hero}} climbed the service ladder to the winch controls. The descent motor was locked to a timer, and the manual brake had been wired to a small recorder. The specialist stopped the tape and heard a dockworker describing the same container arriving years earlier, down to a dent that had not yet happened.

The container struck the upper guide rail and began to swing. {{hero}} held the brake while the dockhands cleared the concourse, then risked one hand to pull the recorder free. A torn corner of manifest slipped under the locked door, naming a sender who was standing on the platform below.

endings.heroWins: The dockhands brought the container down safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept its recorder.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail took the winch and claimed the container when it reached the deck.
endings.draw: The concourse was spared, but both crews watched the container leave again on an empty tether.

paragraphs: The city’s election archive displayed two winners for a vote held only once. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors came for the sealed tally drive; {{otherPlayer}}’s officials arrived with an order to lock the archive until morning. Outside, a crowd waited beneath a public clock whose hands were running backward.

{{hero}} reached the counting desk and found a strip of unprinted ballots threaded through the drive’s cooling fan. The specialist shut down the fan to save the ballots, knowing the drive would overheat within minutes. On the wall monitor, a third winner’s name appeared and vanished before anyone else saw it.

A guard stepped into the doorway as the drive’s casing grew hot. {{hero}} copied the final tally onto a blank ballot, then held the fan still long enough to remove the strip. The public clock struck midnight twice, and both teams turned toward the crowd gathering at the glass doors.

endings.heroWins: The auditors carried the tally outside, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the archive open for witnesses.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officials sealed the room with the drive inside.
endings.draw: Both sides left with conflicting ballots while the crowd waited for a count it could trust.

paragraphs: Surveyors had ringed a crater with listening devices after its walls began pulsing at regular intervals. {{heroPlayer}}’s search party approached from the low ridge; {{otherPlayer}}’s research team held the instruments. Each pulse made the shadows inside the crater point toward the sun.

{{hero}} took the ridge and fired at a searchlight that was pinning the party against the rocks. As the lamp fell, a door appeared in the crater wall where the light had just been. It stood open for the length of one pulse, showing a corridor lined with wet footprints.

The next pulse was already building. {{hero}} watched the research team sprint toward the same door and laid down fire across the slope. A smaller footprint formed in the dust beside the fighter, then another. Whoever had come through the corridor was now climbing the ridge behind them.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party held the crater long enough to see the corridor open again.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers reached the doorway while the search party fell back from the ridge.
endings.draw: The door vanished with the last pulse; both parties followed the new footprints away from the crater.

paragraphs: A derelict proving ground still raised its practice targets each morning, though its control bunker had been abandoned. {{heroPlayer}}’s raiders wanted the bunker’s range maps; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards occupied the observation stand. This morning the targets rose wearing fresh uniforms and carrying real identification tags.

{{hero}} took cover behind a concrete divider and fired toward the stand as a guard tried to restart the moving target rail. The rail stopped with a uniformed figure directly between the two groups. The figure did not duck. Instead, it raised a tag toward the raiders as though asking to be recognized.

The bunker door began closing on a timer. {{hero}} covered the approach while a comrade ran for the controls, then saw the figure step off the rail without disturbing the dust. There was room for one group through the door before it sealed, and the figure was already moving toward them.

endings.heroWins: The raiders entered the bunker with {{heroPlayer}}’s fighter covering the door.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the controls and locked the raiders outside.
endings.draw: Both groups left the bunker sealed; its targets continued marching across the empty range.

paragraphs: A passenger ferry had carried the same eleven people across the channel for three days, returning each time with no memory of the crossing. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to inspect its route log; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor patrol held the landing while the passengers queued again without complaint.

{{hero}} found eleven punched tickets in the engine housing, each stamped with a different year. The specialist set the oldest ticket beside the ferry’s compass. For the first time its needle pointed toward the center of the channel, where a low patch of fog had not moved all morning.

The engine started without a pilot. {{hero}} carried the tickets onto the deck and called for the passengers to stay ashore. One of them stepped aboard anyway, holding an unpunched twelfth ticket. Across the landing, the patrol began drawing in the mooring lines.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators kept the ferry at the dock and learned who held the twelfth ticket.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the ferry as it prepared to leave again.
endings.draw: The ferry departed empty; both parties heard eleven voices calling from the fog.

paragraphs: An orbital junkyard had kept one distress beacon powered long after its ship was stripped. {{heroPlayer}}’s boarding team came for the beacon’s core; {{otherPlayer}}’s salvage crew reached the wreck first. Each time the signal repeated, loose tools drifted toward a sealed maintenance hatch.

{{hero}} covered the hatch from an adjoining hull and fired at a clamp holding the salvage crew’s cutting frame. Freed from the frame, the hatch flexed outward like a breathing chest. The fighter saw a handprint forming on its painted surface from the inside, finger by finger.

The distress beacon changed its message to an invitation. {{hero}} held the corridor while the boarding team tried to disconnect the core. Metal shavings floated between the muzzle and the hatch; a second handprint appeared beside the first just as the crew reached the final cable.

endings.heroWins: The boarding team took the core, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people sealed the hatch behind them.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s salvage crew kept the beacon as the boarding team withdrew through the wreck.
endings.draw: The core went dark in both crews’ hands; the handprints remained on the sealed hatch.

paragraphs: A greenhouse grew a single tree that produced a new kind of fruit every morning. {{heroPlayer}}’s field team came for its root sample; {{otherPlayer}}’s botanists had locked the greenhouse to prevent anything from leaving. Today the branches held small glass bulbs, each containing a sleeping insect.

{{hero}} entered through an irrigation hatch and reached the root bed without breaking a bulb. The specialist uncovered a metal ring around the trunk, stamped with the date of tomorrow’s inspection. Beneath the ring ran a narrow tube carrying warm air up from an inaccessible room below.

One bulb opened as {{hero}} loosened the ring. The insect inside beat against the glass and made the others stir in answer. The field team waited outside with a sample case, while the botanists pressed close to the locked door. The trunk shifted, exposing a stair cut into the soil.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team carried a root sample out before the glass bulbs opened.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s botanists kept the greenhouse closed around the waking insects.
endings.draw: Both parties watched the stair open; neither took a sample before the bulbs began to hatch.

paragraphs: A school was about to be demolished with its teaching archive still inside. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came to copy the last lessons; {{otherPlayer}}’s demolition detail controlled the gates. In the empty classrooms, the desks were arranged for a lesson scheduled to begin in six minutes.

{{hero}} found the lesson server beneath a chalkboard covered with drawings of the same doorway. The specialist started a transfer and heard chairs scrape in a room with no children. A projected pupil appeared at the nearest desk and asked whether anyone had told the families where the shelter door was.

The demolition countdown began outside. {{hero}} followed the drawings to a maintenance panel hiding a stair beneath the classroom floor. The transfer was incomplete, but voices called from below and the gate crew was approaching. The projected pupil pointed toward the stair, then disappeared as the lights dimmed.

endings.heroWins: The stair opened, and {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers led the hidden families out with the lessons saved.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail took the building before the caretakers could finish the transfer.
endings.draw: The families escaped; the archive remained inside when the building was sealed.

paragraphs: A traffic control hub marked a city block as empty even while thousands of people lived there. {{heroPlayer}}’s systems team arrived to restore its address; {{otherPlayer}}’s contractors guarded a new routing board that would send deliveries around the block forever. Residents had begun painting their street numbers on passing vehicles.

{{hero}} found the erased block in a backup map and patched it into a test display. Every residence appeared for an instant, then vanished as a hidden rule applied itself. The specialist traced the rule to an old emergency evacuation code, issued on a day when nobody remembered an evacuation.

The contractors started taking the board offline. {{hero}} held the backup link open with a portable power cell while a resident read the original code from a paper notice found in a drawer. Its final line named a street that did not exist until the morning after the order was signed.

endings.heroWins: The addresses returned, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the hub open for the residents.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s contractors disconnected the board while the block remained missing from every map.
endings.draw: The residents recovered their addresses on paper, but the hub still refused to recognize them.

paragraphs: A memorial amphitheater stood above a sealed crypt whose names had been scraped from every plaque. {{heroPlayer}}’s honor guard came to read them aloud again; {{otherPlayer}}’s detail held the upper seats under a preservation order. A single fresh wreath lay at the foot of the locked crypt.

{{hero}} met a defender in the narrow passage between the seats. The fighter closed before the defender could bring a weapon to bear, forcing a brief struggle against the stone rail. From inside the crypt came a slow knock, answered by another beneath the stage.

The defender stumbled back into the daylight. {{hero}} reached the stage and found a trapdoor pinned shut by the weight of an old statue. Moving it would expose the fighter to the upper seats, but a voice beneath the boards was calling one of the missing names.

endings.heroWins: The trapdoor opened, and {{heroPlayer}}’s guard restored the names before the assembled mourners.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail kept the stage closed while the honor guard withdrew.
endings.draw: Both parties heard the names read from beneath the stage; neither could say who spoke them.

paragraphs: A sealed evidence van arrived at the courthouse with a different license plate on each side. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors sought the case file inside; {{otherPlayer}}’s security team controlled the parking level and a removal order. The trial was due to begin as soon as the van reached the elevator.

{{hero}} opened a service hatch and found two temperature logs for the same journey. One described a refrigerated compartment; the other recorded a passenger breathing inside it. The specialist lifted the inner panel and heard someone tap a courtroom number from behind the insulation.

The elevator doors opened above the van. {{hero}} started cutting through the insulation while the security team rolled a barrier across the exit. A voice inside named the judge, then went silent. The trial clock overhead ticked toward the opening session.

endings.heroWins: The passenger reached the courtroom with {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors and the evidence file intact.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team moved the van before the inspectors could open the compartment.
endings.draw: The passenger escaped, but the van and its disputed records vanished down the service ramp.

paragraphs: A shuttle remained clamped to an empty station berth, broadcasting a request to dock somewhere else. {{heroPlayer}}’s flight crew came to inspect its guidance unit; {{otherPlayer}}’s port authority had sealed the berth after finding no passengers on its arrival list. Inside, warm cups still sat on every tray.

{{hero}} opened the guidance housing and found the shuttle had been landing at this berth for weeks without a recorded departure. The specialist reset the dock clock, and the passenger manifest filled with names that flickered whenever anyone read them aloud. One cup moved across its tray as though the shuttle had begun accelerating.

The clamps released one by one. {{hero}} held the emergency lock against the cabin’s sudden pull while the flight crew searched the seats for a way to stop the departure. At the far end of the cabin, a child’s drawing showed the same berth viewed from a window outside the station.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the shuttle and kept its guidance record for the passengers’ families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s authority closed the berth and took the shuttle into custody.
endings.draw: The shuttle slipped free without a crew; both parties watched its empty windows turn toward home.

paragraphs: A coastal lighthouse went dark with three fishing boats still outside the reefs. {{heroPlayer}}’s emergency patrol climbed from the beach; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the keeper’s house under a disputed order. Someone had removed the lamp’s lens but left its rotation motor running.

{{hero}} covered the path to the tower while a technician carried a portable lens through the exposed courtyard. Shots from the house shattered the stone at the technician’s feet. The fighter returned fire at the upper windows, keeping the courtyard clear long enough for the technician to reach the stair.

The motor turned the empty lamp toward the boats. {{hero}} saw one boat drifting closer to the reef while the technician struggled with the lens above. The fighter held the lower door against a rush from the house, listening for the moment when the beam would finally cut across the water.

endings.heroWins: The beam returned, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol guided all three boats past the reef.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards kept the tower dark while the patrol signaled the boats from shore.
endings.draw: The boats reached harbor, but the damaged lighthouse remained under neither crew’s control.

paragraphs: A mountain shrine had begun sending prayer flags down the valley, each bearing a name nobody remembered writing. {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors came to retrieve the registry kept inside; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians occupied the stone stairs after a landslide exposed an older building beneath them.

{{hero}} met a guardian at the shrine gate, too close for a clean shot and too narrow a space to pass without a fight. The fighter brought a blade up beneath the hanging flags and forced the guardian away from the entrance. One loose flag wrapped around the weapon, its ink still wet.

The registry rested on a stand just inside. {{hero}} found the name from the flag on its newest page and an empty line beneath it. A tremor shook dust from the exposed building under the stairs, and a second flag rose into the air without any wind.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors carried the registry down before the old shrine collapsed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians kept the gate and the registry as the visitors left the mountain.
endings.draw: The registry survived the collapse, but both groups found their own names on its final page.

paragraphs: A walled tea garden hid a cable relay that carried messages between two distant districts. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers came to replace a damaged spool; {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians had locked the garden after discovering messages addressed to people not yet born. The first unread message bore today’s date.

{{hero}} entered beneath the garden’s raised floor and found the damaged cable threaded through a hollow bamboo stem. The specialist joined it to the new spool while overhead footsteps crossed the stones. A test message clicked through the relay, giving instructions to rescue someone from the garden pond.

The pond stood empty except for a single cup floating near its edge. {{hero}} followed the new cable toward the water as the relay tapped out a second message, this time warning that the first was a trap. The couriers waited at the gate, and the technicians were already moving toward the pond.

endings.heroWins: The couriers kept the relay working, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people carried both messages out for comparison.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians secured the garden and disconnected the new spool.
endings.draw: Both parties left the cup floating while the relay continued to send warnings in the dark.

paragraphs: A floodgate opened at noon, exposing an island that appeared on no survey map. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers crossed by skiff to inspect a stone marker; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol watched the only channel back. A narrow bridge on the island ended halfway across the water without a second bank.

{{hero}} measured the marker and found a depth scale carved on its hidden side. The numbers rose as the water fell. The specialist followed the bridge to its broken end, where a metal mooring ring hung over empty air and the skiff’s rope had begun pulling against its knot.

An upstream siren announced the floodgate’s return. {{hero}} fastened the skiff to the ring and carried the measurements toward the engineers, but one member of the party was still beneath the bridge. From the channel, the patrol signaled that the water was already changing direction.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers escaped with the marker’s measurements and kept the channel through the rising water.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the island as the engineers retreated to shore.
endings.draw: Everyone escaped; the island disappeared before either party could explain the bridge.

paragraphs: A nursery on the settlement’s edge held plants from a world that no longer answered its ships. {{heroPlayer}}’s gardeners came to collect a cutting; {{otherPlayer}}’s quarantine team occupied the greenhouse after the ventilation began carrying voices through the neighborhood. Each voice called someone to the door by name.

{{hero}} reached the oldest planter and found roots growing around a buried speaker. The specialist disconnected its power, but the voices continued from the stems above. A cutting taken from the planter quieted one voice; the remaining plants bent toward it as though listening.

Outside, a child recognized the last voice as a parent lost years earlier. {{hero}} sealed the cutting in a transparent case while the child pressed a hand against the glass. The greenhouse vents started to close, and the plants nearest the door lifted their leaves into the path.

endings.heroWins: The cutting reached {{heroPlayer}}’s gardeners, who kept the nursery open to learn whose voices it held.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s quarantine team closed the greenhouse with every plant still inside.
endings.draw: The child heard one final answer; both parties agreed to leave the sealed case between them.

paragraphs: A battery farm at the desert’s edge stored a village’s winter power. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired crew came to replace failing cells; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors had fenced off the compound after noticing that one row of batteries never discharged. The village lights dimmed each time the inspectors tested the row.

{{hero}} found a second set of terminals hidden beneath the sand. The specialist followed their wires to a buried pump drawing from an unmarked aquifer. Whenever the pump ran, the batteries charged and the village well dropped. Both systems had been installed by the same contractor, whose name was scratched from every panel.

The last cell began to swell. {{hero}} disconnected it, then held the pump breaker open while the village’s remaining charge ran through the safe rows. Outside the fence a queue formed at the dry well. The crew had minutes to decide which machine would receive the next turn of the handle.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew stabilized the farm and kept the village’s lights on without draining the well.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors closed the compound while the crew left its repairs unfinished.
endings.draw: The villagers divided the last charge between light and water, with neither crew claiming the farm.

paragraphs: A floating bank vault was being towed through the harbor at low tide. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors were paid to deliver it to a warehouse; {{otherPlayer}}’s customs launch blocked the channel with a seizure order. Neither side knew why the vault’s owner had insisted it remain above water.

{{hero}} covered the towing line from the deck of a tug, firing toward the launch when someone tried to cut it. The vault swung against the quay and an old weld split, revealing a dry space filled with letters instead of money. The nearest envelope bore the tug captain’s name in handwriting they recognized.

The tide turned and the vault began drawing the tug backward. {{hero}} kept the launch away while the captain climbed out to pull the envelope free. Beneath the letters was a ledger wrapped in oilcloth. A customs officer shouted that the owner had died before the vault was built.

endings.heroWins: The tug delivered the vault, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the letters dry for their owners.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers boarded the tug and took the vault into custody.
endings.draw: Both crews saved the letters before the empty vault slipped beneath the tide.

paragraphs: The arena’s armory opened to find every practice weapon replaced with a real one. {{heroPlayer}}’s security crew was contracted to secure the racks; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors had already locked the spectator exits. A youth tournament was due to begin, and the first competitors were gathering outside.

{{hero}} took position in the upper passage and fired at the lock on a shutter that was trapping the armory staff. The shutter rose far enough for them to crawl free. From the empty arena floor came the sound of a starting bell, followed by a voice announcing names absent from the tournament list.

The crew found a second set of competitors waiting beneath the stands with numbered masks over their faces. {{hero}} kept the passage covered while the staff ushered the young entrants away. One masked figure lifted a weapon toward the exit, and the bell rang a second time.

endings.heroWins: The entrants reached safety, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew held the armory until the masks came off.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors took the arena and its unexplained weapons.
endings.draw: The tournament was canceled; neither party could identify the masked competitors who vanished below the stands.

paragraphs: A museum ship was scheduled to be dismantled after its insurance lapsed at sunset. {{heroPlayer}}’s restoration crew arrived with an old ownership certificate; {{otherPlayer}}’s agents carried a newer one. The ship’s engine bell sounded once whenever either certificate was placed on the captain’s table.

{{hero}} checked the hull registry against the old certificate and found its number stamped inside an engine casing that had never been opened. The specialist took an impression while the agents searched the bridge. Beneath the stamp was a second number, registered to a lifeboat missing since the ship’s final voyage.

The dismantling cranes moved into position. {{hero}} followed a narrow cable from the engine bell to a sealed lifeboat locker and found a handwheel on its far side. Turning it would open the locker, but the certificate and the impression lay unguarded on the table above.

endings.heroWins: The locker gave up the missing record, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew won time to preserve the ship.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s agents took the certificates as the cranes began their work.
endings.draw: The cranes stopped for the night; both claims remained on the captain’s table.

paragraphs: A weather dome above the alpine highway reported clear skies while an avalanche buried the road beneath it. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue squad came to reopen the tunnel; {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew kept the dome sealed to protect its instruments. Three drivers were trapped in a vehicle whose horn sounded under the snow.

{{hero}} covered the tunnel entrance while engineers cut into the drift. When an armed figure moved onto the dome’s observation platform, the fighter fired at the empty railing ahead of them, driving them back from the controls. The vehicle’s horn stopped, then sounded in a pattern the rescuers could follow.

A second slide struck the tunnel. {{hero}} held the exposed approach as the engineers pulled one driver through the breach. The remaining two were deeper inside, and the weather dome’s warning siren finally began to sound, minutes after the snow had already fallen.

endings.heroWins: The squad brought all three drivers out, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people held the tunnel for the rescue vehicles.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew secured the dome while the rescue squad withdrew to regroup.
endings.draw: The drivers escaped, but snow closed the highway again before either team could reopen it.

paragraphs: Two chapter houses claimed custody of a reliquary brought to the same monastery under separate sealed orders. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort reached the outer court as {{otherPlayer}}’s escort entered by the cloister. The monks refused to break either seal until the missing abbot returned.

{{hero}} stood at the reliquary stair when a fighter from the other escort tried to pass. Blades met in the narrow turn of the steps. The struggle ended when both heard a bell ringing from the empty abbot’s cell, though its rope had been removed long ago.

The cell door stood open. Inside was the abbot’s cloak, still damp from rain that had stopped a week earlier, and a note directing the escorts to carry the reliquary together. {{hero}} kept a hand on the stair rail as both parties read the note aloud and questioned its signature.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort kept the reliquary and invited the monks to inspect the order.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s escort carried the reliquary through the cloister gate.
endings.draw: Both escorts stayed with the monks until the abbot could be found and the seals opened.

paragraphs: A frontier chapel stood over the colony’s only working transmitter. {{heroPlayer}}’s settlers needed it to call for supplies; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens had set aside the building as a refuge for people fleeing a brush fire. Smoke reached the windows before anyone finished deciding which use came first.

{{hero}} found the transmitter’s antenna cable running through the bell tower. The specialist could send one brief call before the fire damaged its power feed. From the nave came the sound of newcomers seeking shelter, their boots tracking ash across the floor beneath the cable.

The bell rope burned through and the heavy bell began to fall. {{hero}} hauled the antenna cable aside, shielding the transmitter while the settlers guided the arrivals out of its path. The call remained unsent, and the chapel lights flickered as the flames reached the outer wall.

endings.heroWins: The supply call went through, and {{heroPlayer}}’s settlers kept the chapel open as a refuge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens held the refuge while the settlers sought another transmitter.
endings.draw: Everyone found shelter, but the transmitter burned before either group could claim the building.

paragraphs: A civic concert hall kept its voting records inside the pipes of a monumental organ. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to remove them before renovation; {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians claimed the instrument could not be disturbed during a memorial service. The organ began playing before anyone sat at the console.

{{hero}} covered the gallery as a technician reached the pipe housing. A shadow crossed the opposite balcony with a weapon, and the fighter fired to keep it away from the exposed technician. The music changed key. Behind the front rank of pipes, a narrow compartment opened at the sound.

The compartment held a stack of ballots tied with black ribbon. {{hero}} maintained the gallery line while the technician lowered them by cord to the hall floor. The memorial procession entered below, unaware that a scuffle had begun above their heads and that the organ’s final note was still sounding.

endings.heroWins: The ballots reached the investigators, and {{heroPlayer}}’s detail kept the hall open through the service.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians retained the organ and the ballots it concealed.
endings.draw: The service continued; both parties received copies, and the original ballots stayed in the pipes.

paragraphs: A farm settlement’s grain store had been converted into a pilgrimage shelter for the winter. {{heroPlayer}}’s growers came to reclaim its seed bins before planting season; {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants sheltered families who had nowhere else to go. The first seedlings were already sprouting beneath the floorboards.

{{hero}} tested the bins and found the grain warm enough to spoil. The specialist opened the ventilation shafts one by one, carrying each screen outside for cleaning, while families moved their bedding away from the drafts. Beneath the lowest bin lay a dry pocket of viable seed no one had expected.

A storm broke over the settlement and water ran under the shelter door. {{hero}} lifted the seed sacks onto the upper racks as the families helped raise the cots. The last sack was too heavy for one person, and the floor near it gave way to an old drainage channel.

endings.heroWins: The seed survived, and {{heroPlayer}}’s growers kept the store open for the sheltered families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants held the shelter while the growers carried away what little seed they could.
endings.draw: The families saved the grain together and agreed to share the store until spring.

paragraphs: The mountain refuge had one working oxygen recycler and room for half the people climbing toward it. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue patrol reached the outer door with spare filters; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens kept a second group inside. The recycler’s alarm sounded each time the door opened.

{{hero}} covered the exposed stair while a technician brought the filters up. Fire from an overlooking ridge drove the climbers against the rock. The fighter answered from behind an icebound railing, creating a few steps of clear passage while the technician crawled toward the recycler hatch.

A weak voice came through the refuge intercom: someone inside had locked the recycler to protect its remaining air. {{hero}} stayed on the stair as the technician worked the hatch, watching a fresh line of climbers emerge from the whiteout below. The machine’s alarm fell silent before its fans restarted.

endings.heroWins: The filters took hold, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol opened the refuge to every climber it could reach.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens kept the doors sealed while the patrol found shelter farther down the mountain.
endings.draw: The recycler survived, but both groups divided the refuge and its dwindling air for the night.

paragraphs: A sea chapel was losing its foundations to the tide, and the relic displayed inside belonged to a drowned coastal town. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvage team came to secure it before the next surge; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians asked them to leave it for a final service. Water already ran between the front pews.

{{hero}} crossed the flooded nave with a padded case and discovered the relic was a compass fixed to the altar by a chain. Its needle pointed toward an offshore shoal instead of north. The specialist followed the chain to a drain under the altar, where someone had tucked a dry bundle of children’s drawings.

A wave struck the chapel and moved every pew toward the doors. {{hero}} held the compass above the water while the guardians carried the drawings through the aisle. Outside, boats were gathering on the shoal marked by the needle, their lamps forming a circle around something unseen.

endings.heroWins: The drawings and compass reached shore, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the chapel until the last guardian left.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians kept the altar while the salvage team retreated before the surge.
endings.draw: Everyone escaped with part of the record; the compass went down with the chapel.

paragraphs: A bridge between two districts collected tolls long after the city abolished them. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey party came to reopen it; {{otherPlayer}}’s watch held the gate while a crowd waited with old coins. A child found that each coin bought passage for one person who had disappeared years earlier.

{{hero}} took cover in a toll booth and fired at the gate mechanism when a defender moved to lock the waiting crowd inside. The chain jammed halfway down. The fighter glimpsed a woman crossing in the opposite direction, carrying a suitcase whose tag matched a name on the child’s coin.

The crowd surged toward the open gap. {{hero}} kept the crossing clear while the survey party pulled the chain free. The woman reached the booth and offered the fighter the suitcase key, asking them to deliver it to a family that no longer lived in either district.

endings.heroWins: The bridge stayed open, and {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors took the key to its intended family.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch closed the gate before the waiting crowd could cross.
endings.draw: The crowd crossed in both directions; neither side found the woman after the last coin was spent.

paragraphs: A child arrived at a provincial archive with two guardians and two birth certificates. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators sought the original register; {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants asked that the child remain within the archive until the dispute was settled. The child recognized a portrait on the wall but would not say why.

{{hero}} opened the register and found a blank page between records from the same day. Held to the window, the paper showed an erased address beside a sketch of the portrait’s frame. The specialist removed the frame and discovered a small parcel tied with the ribbon from one certificate.

Both guardians reached for the parcel at once. {{hero}} kept it in sight of the child and unwrapped a key, a photograph, and a letter addressed in handwriting the child recognized. Footsteps approached from the front hall, where a third adult had just asked for the child by name.

endings.heroWins: The investigators preserved the records, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the child safe until the letter was read.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants took custody of the archive and its disputed parcel.
endings.draw: The child left with the letter; both groups retained copies and agreed to keep looking.

paragraphs: A fortified granary stood between a hungry district and a convoy bound for another city. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort brought grain to the gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens held the walls for the people inside. A damaged scale at the entrance was counting each sack twice.

{{hero}} held the approach when someone fired from the upper storehouse. The fighter answered from behind a laden cart, stopping the rush toward the convoy without striking the workers still weighing sacks at the gate. One worker pulled the scale apart and found an extra counter wired beneath its dial.

The district’s ration clerk emerged with a ledger showing exactly the missing amount. {{hero}} kept the gate covered while the workers weighed the final sacks by hand. From inside came a call that the granary’s own bins were empty, and the convoy drivers began turning their vehicles around.

endings.heroWins: The grain reached the district, and {{heroPlayer}}’s escort kept the granary supplied through the night.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens controlled the gate and sent the convoy away.
endings.draw: The workers divided the sacks at the gate, leaving both groups with too little and a reason to return.

paragraphs: A postal station on a high pass held letters from people whose villages had vanished under snow. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers wanted to recover the mail; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries guarded the station after fresh tracks appeared around it overnight. The tracks led to the door but never away.

{{hero}} found a ledger beside a cold stove and counted one delivered parcel for each vanished village. The specialist matched the parcel numbers to carved markers along the pass, where the snow had fallen into shallow hollows. A light moved beneath one hollow as a courier stepped toward it.

The courier called from under the snow without falling through. {{hero}} braced a rope against the station wall and led the search to the hollow, where a hidden hatch lifted from below. Inside waited an elderly postmaster with the last undelivered bag and no idea that the villages were gone.

endings.heroWins: The couriers brought out the postmaster and the mail, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the station open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries closed the pass before the couriers could reach the hatch.
endings.draw: Both groups helped the postmaster out; the letters still had no homes to receive them.

paragraphs: A forest observation tower recorded a line of lights moving between trees every night at the same hour. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts came to map their route; {{otherPlayer}}’s watch had sealed the tower after the observer failed to return. His logbook ended halfway through a drawing of a familiar farmhouse.

{{hero}} covered the tower steps as the scouts searched below. A figure moved between the trunks, and the fighter fired into the ground before it to make it stop. The figure kept walking. Its lantern showed the missing observer’s face, though his hands carried the logbook the scouts had just found upstairs.

The lights gathered at the base of the tower. {{hero}} held the stair while the scouts compared the two logbooks, page for page. The final drawing in the one upstairs had changed: the farmhouse was gone, and the observer had sketched a door in its place.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts left with both books and a route to the missing farmhouse.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch kept the tower while the scouts withdrew from the lights.
endings.draw: The tower stood empty by morning, its logbooks still disagreeing over where the farmhouse had been.

paragraphs: A hilltop enclosure was being cleared for a new road while the village prepared its midsummer gathering there. {{heroPlayer}}’s defenders built a gate of timber and rope; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol arrived with the survey stakes. Someone had tied a white sheep to the central post as a warning.

{{hero}} met a survey guard at the narrow gate and fought at arm’s length to keep the stakes out of the enclosure. A blade cut through the rope above them. The central post tilted toward the sheep, which had tangled itself in the falling line.

The fighter broke away to catch the post while another villager freed the animal. {{hero}} planted the timber upright with both hands, seeing the patrol’s stakes scattered across the hill and the first villagers arriving for the gathering. The gate stood open between the two groups.

endings.heroWins: The gathering went ahead, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the hill for the village.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol placed its stakes while the defenders moved the gathering downhill.
endings.draw: The sheep wandered through the open gate, and both sides left their markers until morning.

paragraphs: A refrigerated food depot lost power as relief trucks approached from two directions. {{heroPlayer}}’s dispatch team needed the cold room for medicine; {{otherPlayer}}’s stewards had filled it with food for a stranded neighborhood. The depot’s old ledger offered no way to tell which cargo had arrived first.

{{hero}} found a manual compressor behind stacked crates and began turning it while the others sorted medicine from food. A frost-covered label beneath the lowest crate named a third shipment no one had logged. The specialist followed a thin trail of water to a locked storage door beside the compressor.

A child knocked from inside the storage room. {{hero}} stopped the compressor long enough to hear a reply, then wedged the handle so it would keep turning while the door came open. Behind it were people sheltering from the heat, holding the missing shipment’s blankets around their shoulders.

endings.heroWins: The depot stayed cold, and {{heroPlayer}}’s dispatchers delivered medicine and food together.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s stewards kept the cold room while the dispatchers took the medicine elsewhere.
endings.draw: Both convoys unloaded, but the power failed again before either could take charge of the depot.

paragraphs: A river lock held a recovery capsule that had splashed down far upstream. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to retrieve its flight recorder; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the lockhouse after finding an unopened distress message inside. The capsule’s heat shield still felt warm beneath cold river spray.

{{hero}} opened a maintenance port and found the recorder tangled in reed roots growing through the hull. The specialist freed it as the lock gates began to open on an automatic cycle. Within the recorder’s first seconds was a warning that the capsule had entered the river twice, hours apart.

The lock water surged. {{hero}} tied the recorder to a floating service ring and reached for a technician stranded on the lower walkway. A guard in the lockhouse shouted that the second landing had yet to happen. Above the river, a new trail of fire crossed the evening sky.

endings.heroWins: The technician escaped, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the recorder for the coming landing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the recorder as the capsule passed through the gates.
endings.draw: The recorder floated to shore between the crews while a second capsule fell toward the river.

paragraphs: A factory siren sounded at sunrise although the mill had been closed for decades. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspection squad entered to find the source; {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers controlled the front gate and insisted the building was safe. In the silent workshop, fresh footprints led toward the boiler room.

{{hero}} covered the catwalk while a mechanic checked the siren’s power line. A figure moved below with a weapon, and the fighter fired through the mesh to turn it from the boiler controls. The mechanic found the line unplugged. The siren rang anyway, vibrating dust from the rafters.

A pressure gauge climbed as the workshop lights came on. {{hero}} kept the boiler door in sight while the mechanic opened a relief valve. Through the glass of the factory office, a payroll clock stamped another shift card for a worker whose name had been crossed out years ago.

endings.heroWins: The pressure fell, and {{heroPlayer}}’s squad held the factory while the mechanic traced the siren.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers retook the boiler room and closed the gate.
endings.draw: Both groups left after the pressure eased; the siren sounded again at the next sunrise.

paragraphs: An orchard divided two settlements, and its irrigation tower was the only place their radios could reach one another. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers came to replace the tower battery before the evening freeze; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries guarded it for a funeral procession passing beneath the trees. Every gate in the orchard stood open except the one leading home.

{{hero}} climbed the lattice with the new battery strapped to a line. From above, the specialist saw a wagon wheel sunk in the muddy lane and mourners trying to move the coffin by hand. The old battery began to spark against the tower rail, threatening the radio and everyone directly below it.

A wind shook the ladder while {{hero}} pulled the dead battery clear. The funeral party reached the locked gate and asked for help. The specialist could restore the signal first or lower the battery line to lift the heavy gate; either choice left the other job exposed as darkness settled over the orchard.

endings.heroWins: The gate opened and the tower came back to life, leaving {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers with the orchard crossing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries kept the tower while the funeral party found another road through the trees.
endings.draw: The procession crossed safely, but the radio fell silent and both crews remained to repair it.

paragraphs: A traveling blood bank stopped in the square just as its refrigeration unit failed. {{heroPlayer}}’s medical team wanted the generator beneath the neighboring assembly hall; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens had claimed the hall for a night shelter. The portable fridges held a match for a patient already waiting on the other side of town.

{{hero}} found the hall generator running its lights at full strength, with no spare outlet and a damaged transfer switch. The specialist bridged the switch using an insulated lead from the clinic, then shut down the stage lights one circuit at a time. Families in the hall watched their sleeping area darken as the fridge motors caught.

The patient’s ambulance arrived while the generator began to knock. {{hero}} held the new connection in place and asked the wardens to bring lamps to the families. A medic carried the matching case through the square, but the hall’s emergency alarm tripped before they reached the vehicle.

endings.heroWins: The matching blood stayed cold, and {{heroPlayer}}’s medics left the hall lit for its guests.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens kept the generator while the medics took the last chilled case elsewhere.
endings.draw: The ambulance departed with its case; both groups spent the night rationing power in the hall.

paragraphs: A treaty signed a century ago gave safe passage through the old quarter, but its only surviving copy was being moved from a shuttered library. {{heroPlayer}}’s messengers arrived with the librarian’s key; {{otherPlayer}}’s escorts held the entrance for a delegation. The delegation would have to cross the quarter before sundown.

{{hero}} found the treaty inside a hollow atlas, its pages folded around a pressed sprig of rosemary. The specialist photographed the signature while the librarian listened for footsteps in the reading room. One seal belonged to a family now represented on both sides of the delegation, and each side disputed which name should be read aloud.

The escorts began closing the library shutters. {{hero}} carried the atlas into the narrow hall as the librarian pointed to a second passage, once used by students to reach the public square. The delegation was gathering outside, and the document mattered only if someone could bring it into their hearing.

endings.heroWins: The treaty was read in the square, and {{heroPlayer}}’s messengers kept the passage open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s escorts held the library and delayed the crossing until the delegation withdrew.
endings.draw: Both sides heard the treaty; neither accepted who had the right to enforce its passage.

paragraphs: A pilgrim ship reached the orbital customs ring with one more passenger than its launch record showed. {{heroPlayer}}’s harbor officers sought the original manifest; {{otherPlayer}}’s escorts wanted their passengers through the airlock before the ring closed for inspection. The extra traveler insisted they had boarded with a ticket, not a name.

{{hero}} checked the cargo terminal and found a single seat assigned to a sealed crate. Its mass reading had changed halfway through the voyage. The specialist brought the crate to the inspection bay as the passenger identified a childhood drawing pasted beneath its shipping label, visible only where the paper had torn.

The ring’s lockdown began with the crate still sealed. {{hero}} could break its customs seal and risk delaying every pilgrim, or record the extra traveler without explaining how they arrived. The passenger set the ticket on the inspection table and asked the escorts not to open the crate without them.

endings.heroWins: The manifest was corrected, and {{heroPlayer}}’s officers kept the inspection bay open for the traveler.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s escorts took the passengers and crate beyond the ring before the review ended.
endings.draw: The pilgrims continued their journey, but the unclaimed ticket remained in the customs ledger.

paragraphs: A rescue aircraft landed beside an isolated chapel with four incubators and fuel for one more flight. {{heroPlayer}}’s relief crew needed the building’s sheltered courtyard to stabilize the infants; {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers had turned it into a gathering place for families searching for missing children. The pilot kept the engines warm.

{{hero}} moved a portable monitor into the courtyard and found its power lead too short to reach the chapel outlet. The specialist ran a spare cable through an open window while parents carried tables aside. A handwritten list of missing names hung beside the socket, and one of them matched a tag on an incubator.

The aircraft’s fuel warning sounded. {{hero}} held the monitor steady as the infant’s parent pushed through the crowded entrance, unable to say where they had been during the evacuation. The crew needed a clear path back to the plane, yet no one wanted to separate the family again.

endings.heroWins: The family boarded together, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the courtyard ready for the next rescue.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers controlled the chapel while the aircraft departed with the incubators.
endings.draw: The infants left safely; both parties agreed to keep the missing-name list in the courtyard.

paragraphs: A mural celebrating the city’s founding covered the wall of an abandoned transit terminal. {{heroPlayer}}’s preservation crew came to lift its painted panels; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians claimed the terminal as the last intact memorial to the original settlers. A demolition vehicle waited at the far entrance with its engine running.
