{{hero}} watched from the ticket balcony and fired at the vehicle’s front tire as it rolled toward the crew. It slewed against a pillar without reaching the mural. A loose panel fell away from the wall and revealed a painted second scene beneath: the settlers leaving the city, not entering it.

The crew tried to carry the fallen panel outside while the guardians crossed the hall. {{hero}} held the balcony and kept a clear path past the stalled vehicle. Beneath the last sheet of paint, a date appeared that was older than any record of the terminal’s construction.

endings.heroWins: The preservation crew saved both paintings, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people held the terminal for their study.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians kept the wall while the crew escaped with a single damaged panel.
endings.draw: The vehicle was stopped, but neither side would move the mural until its date was explained.

paragraphs: An outdoor mask festival had taken over the observatory steps just as a once-in-a-century eclipse approached. {{heroPlayer}}’s festival crew needed the rooftop screen to share the event; {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers wanted the steps cleared so their instruments could track it. The crowd refused to leave while the masks still had no faces.

{{hero}} found a safe route for the screen cables along the closed stairwell. The specialist patched the observatory feed into the festival projector and drew a view of the darkening sky across every blank mask. A keeper called from the roof: the main telescope was turning toward an object well away from the sun.

The projector flickered when the eclipse reached its peak. {{hero}} climbed to the distribution box and held a failing connector while the crowd lifted their faces toward the screen. On the roof, the telescope stopped. Whatever it had followed now occupied the edge of the projected image.

endings.heroWins: The screen stayed lit through the eclipse, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the steps open to everyone.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers reclaimed the observatory and ended the festival projection.
endings.draw: The crowd saw the eclipse; neither group could recover the image that appeared beside it.

paragraphs: A maintenance lift stopped between the floors of a domed cathedral with a worker still inside. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers climbed in to bring the lift down; {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians refused to let them cut the load-bearing cable above a crowded vigil. The worker tapped a wrench against the shaft in steady threes.

{{hero}} reached the machinery room and found the lift’s counterweight held by a bent pin. The specialist secured a second line to the drum while the riggers called to the trapped worker below. Each turn of the drum shifted weight through the dome, sending plaster dust across the people at prayer.

The pin slid another inch. {{hero}} locked the drum with both hands as the custodians guided the crowd away from the center aisle. From the shaft came three more taps, then a pause, then a fourth. The lift had moved, and the worker was trying to tell them where.

endings.heroWins: The lift reached the floor, and {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers kept the machinery room safe for repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians kept the building closed as the riggers sought another way into the shaft.
endings.draw: The worker escaped, but both crews left the damaged lift suspended until the vigil ended.

paragraphs: Someone had bought the debt on a neighborhood clinic and sent collectors to close its doors at noon. {{heroPlayer}}’s security contractors came with proof the loan had been paid; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens guarded the sealed accounting room. Patients waited outside with treatment numbers written on their hands.

{{hero}} took cover beside the waiting area and fired at a lockbox trolley as it rolled toward the exit. The trolley tipped without striking the patients. A payment receipt slipped free, bearing the clinic’s stamp beside a signature nobody in the room recognized.

The collectors returned for the box while the nurse tried to match the signature to an old payroll sheet. {{hero}} held the corridor, turning every shot away from the treatment rooms. The clock above admissions approached noon, and one patient’s number was being called for surgery.

endings.heroWins: The receipt kept the clinic open, and {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors held the doors for its patients.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens retained the accounting room and locked the clinic pending review.
endings.draw: The patient received treatment; neither party settled the clinic’s debt before nightfall.

paragraphs: A ring of standing stones had acquired a new stone overnight, smooth and warm in the cold field. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey party came to study it; {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers held the entrance to a nearby sanctuary. During the morning chant, every stone cast a shadow toward the new arrival.

{{hero}} covered the ring from a broken terrace and fired across the path when a team tried to carry a measuring device away. The device struck the ground and began recording a heartbeat from inside the smooth stone. The fighter saw its surface flex, then become still when the chant stopped.

The keepers resumed the chant to test what they had heard. {{hero}} kept the terrace clear while the survey party reached the stone with a portable reader. Its display showed the heartbeat following the voices exactly, and a hand-shaped mark appeared beneath the surface as the final verse began.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party held the ring and preserved the reader’s recording of the heartbeat.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers sealed the field before the survey party could finish its measurements.
endings.draw: The final verse ended; both parties left the new stone where it stood, warm and silent.

paragraphs: A cable station on the plateau kept the villages below in touch with the outside world. {{heroPlayer}}’s repair column arrived after its signal failed; {{otherPlayer}}’s watch occupied the upper gantry, convinced someone had been using the line to summon an armed convoy. A damaged insulator swung above the only safe path to the controls.

{{hero}} covered the approach while two repairers climbed toward the insulator. A shot from the gantry struck the cable housing; the fighter fired back, making room for the repairers to reach the loose fitting. Below them, a trapped operator signaled through the station window that the line still carried power.

A wind gust pulled the live cable across the ladder. {{hero}} kept the gantry under watch as a repairer hooked it away with an insulated pole. The operator wrote a number on the window: the minutes before the lower villages lost their emergency transmitters entirely.

endings.heroWins: The signal returned, and {{heroPlayer}}’s column held the station while the villages called for help.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch kept the gantry and closed the path to the damaged line.
endings.draw: The villages got one brief warning through before both parties disconnected the unsafe cable.

paragraphs: A traveling fair had abandoned its carousel in the plaza, leaving every wooden mount turned toward a chapel door. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to recover the ticket ledger; {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants held the plaza for a vigil. No one could explain why the carousel had kept turning after its power was cut.

{{hero}} opened the control box and found a hand-cranked music roll beneath the motor. Each note lifted a different mount, revealing a number burned into its saddle. The specialist matched the numbers to the ledger and discovered one ticket had been sold for the vigil before the fair arrived.

The carousel slowed when {{hero}} removed the roll. A child stepped forward holding that ticket and asked to ride to the chapel door, as they had been promised. The investigators waited beside the control box while the attendants made room, and the last wooden mount stopped directly in front of the child.

endings.heroWins: The child reached the door, and {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators kept the roll and ledger together.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants closed the plaza after the vigil, leaving the investigators outside.
endings.draw: The vigil ended with the carousel still; the ticket stayed with the child instead of either crew.

paragraphs: A signal relay had been built into the roof of an old stone hospital. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery team came for its transmitter; {{otherPlayer}}’s orderlies guarded the wards below, where failing equipment still sustained several patients. Every relay burst made the monitors skip the same second.

{{hero}} watched the roof approach from a broken stairwell and fired when a defender rushed the transmitter platform. The fighter kept the shots above the ward windows. A recovery worker reached the relay and found its power feed woven through the hospital’s oldest life-support circuit.

Unplugging the transmitter would stop its signal, but the ward monitors would go dark as well. {{hero}} held the stair while the worker ran a bypass cable down toward the orderlies, who had to decide whether to accept it. One patient’s monitor missed its second and did not restart.

endings.heroWins: The bypass held, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team carried the transmitter away without silencing the ward.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s orderlies kept the relay connected while the recovery team withdrew.
endings.draw: The patients remained stable; the relay stayed in place under a watch shared by both groups.

paragraphs: A row of farms disappeared from the cadastral map, though their houses still stood along the road. {{heroPlayer}}’s field team came to locate the boundary marker; {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers guarded the last farm’s well. Each family remembered a different date for the day the land had been surveyed.

{{hero}} found a buried survey pin beneath the well cover. Its serial number belonged to a later survey, one completed after the fields had vanished from official records. The specialist copied the number while a farmer unfolded a deed whose ink changed color whenever it crossed the well’s shadow.

The pump started without anyone touching it, sending muddy water over the deed. {{hero}} lifted the paper out of reach and read an address exposed where the color had washed away. It named a house just beyond the field, visible to both teams but empty when the farmer called home.

endings.heroWins: The field team carried the pin and deed away, leaving {{heroPlayer}}’s people in control of the disputed well.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers held the well and refused to release the survey pin.
endings.draw: The families kept the deed; both teams agreed the missing house needed a new survey.

paragraphs: A city’s flood barriers began closing against a storm that had not yet reached the coast. {{heroPlayer}}’s control team came to inspect the forecast engine; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians held the pump station to keep its lower neighborhood dry. Boats loaded along the canal while the sky stayed blue.

{{hero}} found the engine using an old map on which an entire street had been replaced by a river. The specialist corrected the map and watched the barrier schedule change, then found a handwritten note under the console warning that this error had saved lives once before.

The canal level rose while {{hero}} compared the new schedule to the note. A drainage crew called from the endangered street: water was seeping up through basement floors rather than arriving from the sea. The specialist left the barriers half closed, holding the decision until the crew could reach higher ground.

endings.heroWins: The barriers held where they were needed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the pump station running.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians took the controls and followed the old flood schedule.
endings.draw: The residents escaped the basements; both groups remained to watch a river that was not on the map.

paragraphs: A public memory wall had stopped showing the names of workers who built the city’s first shelter. {{heroPlayer}}’s archivists came to restore the display; {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers held the plaza during an anniversary gathering. The missing names had been replaced by photographs of faces turned away from the camera.

{{hero}} followed the display cable to a maintenance alcove and found a second memory card with the names intact. Its timestamp was tomorrow’s date. The specialist connected it to a spare screen for the caretakers to inspect, but the photographs changed as soon as the first name appeared.

A woman in the gathering recognized her father’s coat in one of the photographs. {{hero}} kept the spare screen powered while she looked for his face, turning through the names one by one. The anniversary speech began, and the crowd faced the wall, waiting to see whether its missing builders would return.

endings.heroWins: The names returned to the wall, and {{heroPlayer}}’s archivists kept the plaza display working.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers held the wall while the archivists left with the undated card.
endings.draw: The crowd read the names on the spare screen; the main wall remained blank after the gathering.

paragraphs: A field of white tents marked the ground where two armies once agreed to exchange their wounded. {{heroPlayer}}’s honor party arrived with a memorial stone; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens claimed the tents were still needed for living patients. A stretcher lay at the center of the field, unattended but moving slightly beneath its sheet.

{{hero}} met a fighter at the rope line and struggled blade to blade for a clear path to the stretcher. Neither could step aside without entering the occupied tents. The sheet stirred again; someone beneath it called a name recognized by the oldest medic in the camp.

The medic pushed between the fighters. {{hero}} lowered the blade and held the rope line while the sheet came back to reveal a wounded courier still clutching a delivery tube. The tube bore the date of the original ceasefire, and the courier asked whether the exchange had finally begun.

endings.heroWins: The courier reached care, and {{heroPlayer}}’s honor party placed the stone beside the living tents.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens kept the field and delayed the memorial.
endings.draw: The courier was treated; both parties carried the stone to the edge of the tents together.

paragraphs: A small embassy stood between two jurisdictions, its front door on one street and its back door on another. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors arrived to protect a witness waiting inside; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards had orders to keep the building sealed until a transfer warrant could be checked. The witness would only speak before sunset.

{{hero}} examined the warrant against the embassy’s boundary plan and found that its seal covered a handwritten correction. Under the seal was the wrong street. The specialist photographed the correction in the witness’s presence while a clerk tried to contact the judge who had signed it.

At sunset the back door began closing on a timer. {{hero}} held the hinge with a portable brace so the witness could see both streets from the threshold. The clerk returned with an answer: the judge had never seen the corrected address, and someone outside was already trying to remove the brace.

endings.heroWins: The witness gave a statement, and {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors kept the embassy open under a valid order.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards sealed the building while the warrant was disputed.
endings.draw: The witness spoke to both groups at the threshold; jurisdiction remained unsettled after dark.

paragraphs: An evacuation shuttle reached the station’s oldest docking arm with one engine still burning. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock patrol came to clear a path for its passengers; {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians held the gate to an infirmary already beyond capacity. The shuttle hatch would open before anyone could bring another stretcher.

{{hero}} covered the gangway from a maintenance recess, firing at a barricade wheel to keep it from rolling across the passengers’ route. The wheel jammed against a rail. An injured pilot stepped out and pointed back toward the engine, where a thin line of coolant was creeping toward the air intake.

The dock patrol moved the passengers past the stopped barricade. {{hero}} kept the gangway clear while a mechanic reached the engine valve. From the infirmary came a request for beds the station did not have, and the shuttle’s final passenger emerged carrying a folded stretcher rather than lying on it.

endings.heroWins: The engine was made safe, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol brought every passenger through the dock.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians closed the infirmary gate while the patrol sought shelter elsewhere.
endings.draw: The passengers escaped the shuttle, but both groups had to build a ward on the gangway.

paragraphs: A rescue train stopped inside the mountain tunnel with its lamps still lit but no radio contact. {{heroPlayer}}’s search patrol entered from the lower portal; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries controlled the ventilation station above. Passengers had marked arrows on the windows, all pointing toward a locked service door.

{{hero}} covered the platform cut into the tunnel wall while a mechanic worked the door. A figure moved behind the upper vents, and the fighter fired at the grate to hold it back. The grate fell open, letting in cold air and the distant sound of someone calling from a shaft beyond the tracks.

The mechanic freed the lock as smoke gathered near the rear carriage. {{hero}} held the open grate under watch while passengers stepped through the service door one at a time. The last person refused to leave, insisting a companion was still in the shaft where the voice had called.

endings.heroWins: The search patrol found the missing passenger and held the tunnel until {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue train could leave.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries kept the ventilation station while the patrol withdrew with those it had rescued.
endings.draw: The passengers escaped, but neither group found the voice in the dark shaft.

paragraphs: A shipyard chapel kept a lantern burning for crews who never returned. {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors came to carry it in a harbor procession; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians occupied the slipway after discovering an unfinished vessel there. The lantern’s glass held names etched so faintly they appeared only when its flame moved.

{{hero}} met a defender at the narrow gangplank, where neither could step aside without falling between the hull and the quay. Steel crossed above the water. The fighter won enough room for the procession to reach the lantern, then saw its flame bend toward a name that had not been there when the visitors arrived.

A woman at the front recognized the new name as her brother’s, though his boat was due in the morning. {{hero}} held the gangplank while she lifted the lantern and turned it toward the harbor. Far out in the mist, a single answering light changed course.

endings.heroWins: The procession reached the shore, and {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors kept the lantern lit for the returning boat.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians held the slipway and returned the lantern to its chapel.
endings.draw: Both groups saw the boat’s light; the lantern stayed between them until morning.

paragraphs: Monsoon water entered a hillside monastery through a stair no one could find on the floor plan. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers came for an old map stored in its cellar; {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians carried valuables toward the upper rooms. The map could show a dry way out for the villagers below.

{{hero}} followed the water through a tiled corridor and found the missing stair behind a movable screen. The specialist rescued a lacquered map case just as the lower steps disappeared beneath the flood. Its painted trail crossed the monastery courtyard, then ended at a well marked with a symbol no one recognized.

The custodians began closing the courtyard gate against the rising water. {{hero}} held the map open for them beneath a roof eave while a villager climbed through the well’s old service opening. The trail went under the wall, and the next person through would have to carry the map into the dark.

endings.heroWins: The villagers followed the route, and {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers kept the map safe above the flood.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians retained the monastery and its map as the couriers withdrew.
endings.draw: The villagers escaped by the well, leaving both crews to argue over the damaged original.

paragraphs: A clockmaker’s square had four public clocks, all showing a different hour on the day its founder was to be commemorated. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey detail came to repair the central bell; {{otherPlayer}}’s watch held the tower stairs for the ceremony. Shopkeepers insisted each clock was correct for their side of the square.

{{hero}} covered the tower from a shuttered workshop and fired at a hinge when a guard moved to seal the stairs. The door swung back open. A clockmaker’s apprentice emerged with a gear that had four sets of teeth, each matched to one of the clocks, and begged for a moment to fit it.

The ceremony began as the apprentice climbed. {{hero}} kept the stairs clear and watched the hands around the square move together for the first time. The bell rope jerked from an unseen pull above, threatening to strike before the apprentice reached the mechanism.

endings.heroWins: The bell sounded at the agreed hour, and {{heroPlayer}}’s detail held the tower through the ceremony.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch closed the stairs and set the clocks without the survey detail.
endings.draw: All four clocks agreed for one minute; neither party could keep them synchronized afterward.

paragraphs: A rare flowering vine grew across the roof of a neutral meeting house. {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists came to preserve its only viable cutting; {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers wanted the meeting to continue beneath the shade it provided. The petals opened for only an hour each year, and rain was already gathering beyond the valley.

{{hero}} climbed the roof trellis and found a cluster of unopened flowers wrapped around a cracked skylight. The specialist braced the glass before reaching for a cutting. Through the skylight, delegates below struggled to hear one another over the first drops of rain, unaware that the trellis had begun to sag.

A wooden support gave way. {{hero}} secured the vine with the carrying line meant for the cutting and called for help from the meeting floor. The petals opened as the delegates reached the skylight; saving the flowers now meant letting the cutting wait until the roof was safe.

endings.heroWins: The roof held and the cutting survived, leaving {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists to tend the meeting house.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers retained the vine while the botanists left without a cutting.
endings.draw: The delegates saved the roof together; the brief flowering passed before anyone could take a sample.

paragraphs: A temporary market had grown around a field radio mast, its awnings tied to every support cable. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired escorts came for a stranded broadcaster; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens occupied the stall beside the transmitter. A public warning was halfway through when someone began cutting the guy ropes.

{{hero}} took cover beneath a spice stall and fired into the cobbles ahead of the cutters, scattering them without hitting the traders. One awning fell across the broadcaster’s doorway. The mast swayed above the crowd as the warning continued, now naming the market itself as the danger.

The fighter held the approach while merchants pulled the fallen fabric aside. The broadcaster stepped out carrying a hand microphone and asked {{hero}} for thirty more seconds. Above them another guy rope snapped, and the remaining stalls began to slide toward the unsteady mast.

endings.heroWins: The warning went out and the traders cleared the square under {{heroPlayer}}’s escort.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took the transmitter while the escorts led the broadcaster away.
endings.draw: The mast fell in the empty square; both groups saved the traders but lost the signal.

paragraphs: A border warehouse held aid parcels for a town whose access road had vanished in a landslide. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors had been hired to move the supplies by rail; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians held the loading doors until the sender could be verified. Each parcel carried a handwritten destination but no return address.

{{hero}} covered the loading platform as a forklift approached from the wrong end of the track. The fighter fired at its empty wheel housing, turning it away from workers stacking crates. One package spilled open and revealed a child’s winter coat with a school badge from the isolated town.

The rail wagon was nearly full when the warehouse lights went out. {{hero}} stayed between the workers and the darkened doors while a foreman found the manual gate chain. Beyond the yard a train whistle sounded, promising one trip before the repaired road reopened.

endings.heroWins: The train carried the parcels, and {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors kept the platform until the final wagon left.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians held the warehouse while the contractors lost their rail window.
endings.draw: The coats reached the town; both parties stayed to sort the unclaimed parcels.

paragraphs: A coastal salvage depot had taken in a sealed lifeboat after a storm. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors arrived to collect its emergency transmitter; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians held the depot until the boat’s crew could be identified. A maintenance light blinked inside the sealed hull whenever someone tried the door.

{{hero}} covered the crane yard when a defender moved to swing a cargo hook over the contractors’ approach. The fighter fired at the crane’s empty control housing, stopping the hook clear of the lifeboat. A mechanic cut through the seal and found every seat occupied by a neatly folded raincoat.

The transmitter clicked on as the mechanic lifted the last coat. {{hero}} held the yard while the crew listened to a distress call from the boat’s registered position, still far out at sea. The tide was rising, and the contractors had to choose between the transmitter and a rescue launch.

endings.heroWins: The rescue launch departed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors kept the transmitter working at the depot.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians secured the boat and its transmitter before a launch could be readied.
endings.draw: Both groups sent a launch; the lifeboat remained empty when its call sounded again.

paragraphs: A hilltop listening station intercepted a call from an expedition missing for six months. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors held a recovery agreement for the recording; {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians kept the station open to the families waiting for news. The call began with a weather report from the morning the expedition disappeared.

{{hero}} reached the recording desk and found its tape almost at the end. The specialist threaded a spare reel through the machine while the families took turns recognizing voices. Beneath the weather report came three knocks and an address that had once belonged to the station itself.

The wind tore the antenna loose during the transfer. {{hero}} held the tape in place as a technician climbed the mast to restore reception. The expedition leader began to speak, then paused for someone beside them to answer. In the listening room, a family member answered the pause aloud.

endings.heroWins: The whole call was saved, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the station available to the families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guardians retained the recording while the contractors withdrew.
endings.draw: Each party kept part of the call; neither could identify the place named in its final seconds.

paragraphs: A mountain checkpoint kept a snowbound convoy waiting while the last driver searched for a missing passenger. {{heroPlayer}}’s support crew came to open a warm shelter; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries held it for a medical delivery due through the pass. A set of footprints stopped at its locked rear wall.

{{hero}} inspected the shelter’s ventilation plan and found an unused hatch behind a stack of fuel drums. The specialist followed the footprints through it to a maintenance alcove, where the missing passenger sat beside a frozen heater. They had gone inside to leave space for a child on the convoy’s last heated seat.

The shelter heater caught when {{hero}} restarted its pilot. Outside, the medical delivery arrived, and the sentries asked for the alcove to unload supplies. The missing passenger rose unsteadily; the convoy’s drivers began carrying blankets through the open hatch before anyone settled who owned the room.

endings.heroWins: The convoy warmed its passengers, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the shelter open for the delivery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries took the shelter as the convoy continued toward the next pass.
endings.draw: Both groups shared the heater through the night, with the checkpoint closed until morning.

paragraphs: Two settlement crews carried different land grants to the same canyon spring. {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors set their instruments above the western bank while {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors marked the eastern path. Neither grant mentioned the fossil beds visible beneath the clear water, each showing a creature curled around something bright.

{{hero}} reached the original boundary stone underwater with a weighted measuring line. The specialist found an older line engraved along its base, running directly through the spring. Each crew gathered on a bank to watch the reading, and both knew moving the stone would erase the only shared reference.

A tremor clouded the spring with silt. {{hero}} held the line against the current while the other surveyors pulled back from falling rock. The bright object inside the nearest fossil reflected the afternoon sun once, and the two crews called out different measurements at the same moment.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the spring and recorded the old line before the water cleared.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew secured the spring and the exposed boundary stone.
endings.draw: Both crews copied the measurement; neither accepted a boundary through the spring.

paragraphs: The colony’s first school occupied a prefab block scheduled for replacement by a larger campus. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspection detail arrived with the new building plans; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept children inside the old classrooms until a safe route across the construction site was marked. One wall had begun to bow toward the playground.

{{hero}} covered the site as workers hurried to brace the failing wall. A machine moved toward the playground with its driver’s cab empty, and the fighter fired at the exposed control panel to stop it short of the children’s gate. The engine died, but the machine’s weight blocked the only marked path.

Teachers began leading children around the stopped machine. {{hero}} watched the unstable wall while a worker pulled the machine’s brake clear. The oldest pupil returned for a class project still drying near the doorway; above that doorway, the first brace started to bend.

endings.heroWins: The pupils reached safety, and {{heroPlayer}}’s detail held the site for repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the school grounds while the inspectors withdrew.
endings.draw: The school emptied safely, but both parties delayed construction until the old wall could be saved.

paragraphs: An earthquake exposed the colony’s gas line beneath a row of new houses. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers came to isolate the break; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the block while their neighbors gathered possessions. A kitchen light flickered on in one empty house just as a detector sounded outside.

{{hero}} reached the junction box by crawling under a tilted porch. The specialist closed one valve, then found a second feed supplying the community kitchens across the street. Shutting both would make the line safe but leave the kitchens dark while food spoiled in their warm storage.

The porch shifted, trapping the junction handle against the wall. {{hero}} asked a settler to hold a brace while turning the valve a fraction at a time. Across the road, cooks carried their last hot trays outside for the evacuated families, watching the detector’s warning light flash faster.

endings.heroWins: The leak was sealed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers kept the block safe for the returning families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers retained the junction while the engineers backed away from the unstable porch.
endings.draw: The families ate together outside; both groups left the houses empty until the line could be replaced.

paragraphs: A survey rover froze halfway across an ice shelf with its sample canisters still warm. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery patrol approached from the high ridge; {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists had tied a towline from the far camp. Each crew needed the rover intact, but a widening crack ran between them.

{{hero}} held the ridge while a mechanic advanced with a replacement power cell. Fire struck the snow near the rover’s antenna, and the fighter answered from behind a rock outcrop to keep the mechanic moving. The rover’s wheels began turning as the new cell connected, dragging the towline across the crack.

The mechanic stumbled when the ice split beneath the line. {{hero}} kept the approach covered while the recovery patrol pulled them toward firm ground. Across the shelf the colonists braced their towline, and the rover moved slowly between both teams with its canisters still heating inside.

endings.heroWins: The patrol brought in the rover and kept the samples cold beneath {{heroPlayer}}’s shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists pulled the rover across to their camp.
endings.draw: Both crews saved the mechanic; the rover dropped into the crack with its samples.

paragraphs: A desalination plant had begun drawing living coral into its coastal intake, coloring the colony’s drinking water pink. {{heroPlayer}}’s divers came to clear the screens; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers guarded the reservoir above the plant. Families had already filled every spare container ahead of a forecasted dry week.

{{hero}} opened the underwater maintenance gate and saw that the coral had formed a wall around a small sealed canister. The specialist lifted it free without tearing the branches. Inside was a handwritten tide chart, wrapped so carefully that its last page remained dry despite the pressure outside.

The intake pump restarted automatically while {{hero}} was still below. The diver held the gate open for a second teammate and passed the chart toward the surface. A pink plume reached the reservoir pipe, and the settlers called down that the morning water allocation was about to begin.

endings.heroWins: The water ran clear, and {{heroPlayer}}’s divers kept the intake open for the colony.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers controlled the plant while the divers withdrew with the tide chart.
endings.draw: The coral survived and the water cleared, but both groups closed the intake pending a new survey.

paragraphs: A freight lift served the cliffside settlement until its counterweight slipped during the morning delivery. {{heroPlayer}}’s response team reached the top station; {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists waited below with grain already loaded. The lift hung over the homes with its door open and a driver still at the controls.

{{hero}} covered the upper platform as a figure tried to cut the emergency cable. The fighter fired into the platform railing ahead of them, turning them back without striking the lift. A mechanic reached the winding drum, where a broken tooth caught every third turn and shook the cabin.

The driver shouted that the grain was shifting toward the open door. {{hero}} kept the platform clear while the mechanic fitted a temporary brace into the drum. At the bottom, colonists stretched a loading net between two rooftops, preparing for the driver whether the cabin moved or not.

endings.heroWins: The lift settled safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the upper station for repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists took the lift controls as the response team withdrew.
endings.draw: The driver reached the net, but both groups left the freight cabin hanging until a new counterweight arrived.

paragraphs: The settlement registry listed a visitor who had never arrived, yet every household had a different memory of offering them supper. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to compare the records; {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists held the town hall for a vote on whether to close the settlement road. At the desk lay a coat nobody claimed.

{{hero}} traced the visitor’s signature across three guest books and found that each had been signed on the same date, in a different hand. The specialist turned the coat inside out and discovered tickets for all three households sewn into its lining, each valid for the following evening.

The vote began while {{hero}} carried the tickets toward the hall. One voter recognized their own handwriting on a ticket they had never seen. A knock sounded at the locked front door, and the clerk asked whether the investigators would let the visitor speak before the road was closed.

endings.heroWins: The visitor entered under {{heroPlayer}}’s protection, and the registry stayed open through the vote.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists closed the road while the investigators kept the coat as evidence.
endings.draw: The road stayed open for one night; no one at the hall admitted owning the coat.

paragraphs: A quarry at the edge of the colony exposed a buried shelter just before its next scheduled blast. {{heroPlayer}}’s safety team came to stop the charges; {{otherPlayer}}’s miners held the pit because their equipment was still inside. Through a small window in the shelter door, someone held up a light.

{{hero}} covered the quarry rim while a technician reached the blast controller. A figure ran toward the detonator line, and the fighter fired into an empty crusher chute to force them back. The light behind the shelter window blinked twice, then traced a number in the dust on the glass.

The number matched the minutes remaining on the blast timer. {{hero}} kept the line clear as the technician disconnected one charge after another. A miner climbed into the pit with a cutting torch; the shelter door had swollen shut, and its light was fading.

endings.heroWins: The charges stayed silent, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team opened the shelter before the light went out.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s miners kept the quarry controls while the safety team retreated.
endings.draw: The shelter opened, but both groups postponed the blast until its occupant could be identified.

paragraphs: A wildlife corridor crossed the colony’s new access road. {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers came to mark a safe crossing; {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew had laid the first foundation that morning. Small tracks in the wet concrete showed that an animal had already crossed while the workers’ backs were turned.

{{hero}} followed the tracks to a culvert and found two young animals trapped behind a fallen survey panel. The specialist lifted the panel and fitted a tracking marker to its frame, making the culvert visible on the road crew’s maps. Their parent waited on the opposite side of the foundations, watching without approaching.

The concrete truck returned before the crossing was clear. {{hero}} waved it back and guided the young animals through the culvert as the crew removed its outer formwork. The parent stepped forward at last, just as the first concrete started flowing toward the unfinished edge.

endings.heroWins: The animals crossed safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers kept the corridor marked for future traffic.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew closed the roadbed before the trackers could establish the crossing.
endings.draw: The animals escaped; both groups left the road unfinished until a permanent culvert was planned.

paragraphs: A survey camp on the open steppe reported a drilling crew missing after its mast struck a hollow layer of stone. {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers arrived along the ridge; {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists occupied the camp and kept the drill running to reach trapped voices below. The borehole made a low note whenever the bit stopped.

{{hero}} covered the rig while searchers moved to the mast. A warning shot from the camp struck its support, and the fighter returned fire at an empty fuel drum to turn the shooter away. A rescuer climbed the ladder and heard three knocks beneath the engine, separate from the trapped voices.

The drill seized with a crew member still below its platform. {{hero}} kept the ridge clear as the rescuers lowered a spare cable into the hollow stone. The first person to emerge carried a marked survey slate that showed an exit beneath the camp, not the borehole.

endings.heroWins: The missing crew reached the ridge, and {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers held the camp for recovery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists controlled the rig while the searchers withdrew with the survey slate.
endings.draw: The crew escaped through the hidden exit; both groups left the drill silent above it.

paragraphs: A grazing valley had been chosen for the colony’s new fence line, straight through the path used for the seasonal cattle drive. {{heroPlayer}}’s herders came to open the old gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s survey party held it until the boundary posts could be set. The cattle gathered in the narrowing lane behind them.

{{hero}} reached the gate as a survey guard stepped into the way. There was no space for a shot with animals pressing against the rails, so the fighter met the guard at arm’s length and forced a passage by the latch. The herd’s lead animal pushed forward before the hinges were fully free.

The gate came loose in {{hero}}’s hands. The fighter held it upright while the herders guided the first animals through, each passing close enough to brush the broken hinge. Across the valley, the surveyors raised another post where the old path turned toward water.

endings.heroWins: The herd reached water, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the valley path open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors closed the boundary and sent the drive toward the longer pass.
endings.draw: The cattle crossed; both groups returned the next day to move the fence away from the gate.

paragraphs: A border watch cabin overlooked the narrow trail used to bring mail into the colony. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts arrived after the courier failed to report; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers had sheltered the courier’s horse but could not find its rider. The cabin window was open and a fresh map lay pinned under an empty lantern.

{{hero}} took the ridge above the cabin as a figure moved between the pine trunks. When a shot hit the mailbag left on the porch, the fighter answered toward a rock face clear of the horse and the settlers, holding the trail while a scout reached the cabin door. Inside, a boot was wedged against a hidden floor hatch.

The scout pulled the hatch open and found the courier beneath the floor, shielding a bundle of undelivered letters. {{hero}} kept the tree line covered while the settlers ran for a stretcher. On the map, a newly drawn route avoided the trail entirely and led toward smoke rising beyond the ridge.

endings.heroWins: The courier reached safety, and {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts held the cabin while the mail went on.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the cabin as the scouts withdrew toward the smoke.
endings.draw: The letters were delivered, but both crews left the newly drawn route unexplored.

paragraphs: A tethered weather balloon above the colony’s orchard began reporting snow in the middle of harvest. {{heroPlayer}}’s observers came for its instruments; {{otherPlayer}}’s growers needed the forecast before deciding whether to pick early. The balloon cast a moving shadow across rows where the fruit had ripened on only one side.

{{hero}} reached the winch and read the balloon’s pressure record as its tether unwound. The specialist discovered that the sensors had been recording weather from a valley hundreds of kilometers away. A second cable, hidden under the orchard soil, led toward an abandoned listening box on the hill.

The winch brake failed when the first cold gust reached the trees. {{hero}} wrapped the tether around a post and called for the growers to clear the lower rows. At the listening box, a lamp switched on and the forecast changed to a warning meant for the orchard itself.

endings.heroWins: The warning reached the growers, and {{heroPlayer}}’s observers kept the balloon tethered above the orchard.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s growers took the winch while the observers retreated to examine the listening box.
endings.draw: The harvest was saved, but the balloon broke free before either crew could recover its instruments.

paragraphs: A stone bridge gave the colony its shortest route to winter stores, until a landslide cut the path at both ends. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol arrived to secure the crossing; {{otherPlayer}}’s builders were already testing its damaged supports. A wagon remained stranded on the bridge with its driver guarding a crate of medicine.

{{hero}} covered the open approach from a ledge when a figure began loosening the last brace under the wagon. The fighter fired at the empty edge of the stonework to force them away. The bridge shifted nonetheless, leaving the driver pinned between the wagon and a broken parapet.

The builders fed a rope over the gap while {{hero}} watched the far bank. The driver passed the crate across first, then reached for the rope as loose stones fell into the ravine. Behind the patrol, the landslide moved again and erased their own retreat path.

endings.heroWins: The driver and medicine reached firm ground, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol kept the crossing open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s builders took the bridge while the patrol found a longer route home.
endings.draw: Both sides saved the driver; the bridge fell after the final rope was removed.

paragraphs: The colony drilled a new well beside a working oil derrick, and the first bucket came up smelling of fuel. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers arrived to trace the leak; {{otherPlayer}}’s drilling crew guarded the pumps, certain their equipment was sound. The settlement’s water wagon was due to leave at dawn with empty tanks.

{{hero}} followed the contamination to an old pipe buried under a storage shed. The specialist found its valve handle missing and a thin line of clean water running past it, separated by one corroded wall. The rangers marked a safe channel while the drilling crew searched for a tool to turn the valve stem.

Pressure climbed as {{hero}} gripped the stem with a wrench. The shed floor began to lift, and the clean-water line shook beside the fuel pipe. Across the yard the wagon driver opened the tanks, waiting to know whether the next bucket would be safe enough to carry.

endings.heroWins: The wagon filled with clean water, and {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers kept the well under watch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the pumps while the rangers closed the well as unsafe.
endings.draw: The leak stopped, but both parties waited for another test before sending the wagon out.

paragraphs: A caravan of field medics stopped at a colony food hall after its cooks fell ill at once. {{heroPlayer}}’s team needed the kitchen for treatment; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers wanted the hall kept open to feed everyone waiting outside. The first patients had eaten different dishes but shared the same drinking cups.

{{hero}} examined the washing station and found a cracked reservoir beneath its counter. The specialist closed its feed, then asked the cooks to bring every used cup into the courtyard. A gardener recognized the mineral residue on their rims from a spring behind the hall, usually considered too bitter to drink.

The kitchen’s last clean pot was already on the fire. {{hero}} tested the water as a line formed for supper, explaining what might have made the cooks sick. The settlers brought sealed stores from their homes, but the medics still needed the hall’s table space for the patients.

endings.heroWins: The patients received care and supper, and {{heroPlayer}}’s medics held the hall until the water was safe.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the hall while the medics treated patients from their caravan.
endings.draw: Both groups shared the hall through the night, with the spring closed for testing.

paragraphs: A parcel of farmland changed hands three times on the same afternoon, each buyer holding a stamped deed. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to inspect the sale ledger; {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists had already planted seedlings along the new boundary. The disputed plot included a small cemetery no deed mentioned.

{{hero}} found the original ledger at a caravan stop and matched its entries to a carved date on the cemetery wall. The specialist noticed that one deed transferred only the surface land; its missing second page reserved everything beneath the graves for an owner whose name had been rubbed away.

A surveyor began setting posts in the cemetery path. {{hero}} carried the ledger out where both buyers could see it and asked the colonists to halt the digging. The cemetery gate opened from inside, and a caretaker brought out the missing page folded beneath a stone marker.

endings.heroWins: The graves stayed undisturbed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators kept the ledger for a fair hearing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists retained the plot while the investigators withdrew with a copy of the deed.
endings.draw: The seedlings remained outside the cemetery; neither side could establish ownership of the ground beneath it.

paragraphs: A customs island at the mouth of the colony river kept a generator running for boats that crossed after dark. {{heroPlayer}}’s harbor detail came to secure its fuel; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers had stored emergency supplies beside the same engine. A lantern on the upper landing blinked an unfamiliar channel code.

{{hero}} watched the landing from a shuttered control room and fired at the empty winch arm when an intruder tried to lower the fuel barge away from the dock. The barge drifted only a few meters. A boat answered the lantern code from the far shore, carrying passengers who had no other landing.

The generator sputtered as the passengers approached. {{hero}} kept the dock in sight while an engineer switched the beacon to a reserve battery. The barge line strained against the current, and the passengers called for guidance before their boat slid beyond the last marker.

endings.heroWins: The passengers landed safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s detail kept the island beacon lit.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers retained the fuel and took responsibility for the landing.
endings.draw: The passengers reached shore; both crews shared the last fuel until a new shipment arrived.

paragraphs: The colony greenhouse became a field clinic when a survey team returned with severe burns. {{heroPlayer}}’s medics needed its cooling system; {{otherPlayer}}’s growers feared losing a season of seedlings if the vents stayed open. A burned surveyor kept repeating the name of a place absent from their route map.

{{hero}} rigged a misting line beside the treatment beds and narrowed the vents so the seedlings would not freeze. The specialist examined a shard caught in the surveyor’s sleeve: black glass with a compass line etched across it. The remaining surveyors claimed they had found it beneath a field that had never been dug.

The cooling pump seized as the beds filled. {{hero}} turned its flywheel by hand while a grower fetched parts from the nursery. The surveyor opened their eyes long enough to point beyond the greenhouse, where a survey stake stood in ground the growers had fenced off years earlier.

endings.heroWins: The patients stabilized, and {{heroPlayer}}’s medics kept the greenhouse working without losing its crop.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s growers reclaimed the greenhouse while the medics moved the patients to their transport.
endings.draw: The seedlings and patients survived; both groups waited for the surveyors to explain the stake.

paragraphs: A recycling barge arrived at the colony dock carrying equipment from a ship officially lost in transit. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvage crew came to inventory the load; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers guarded the pier until the missing crew could be accounted for. Fresh food wrappers lay among the sealed crates.

{{hero}} covered the barge ramp as a figure on the far pier moved to cut its mooring. The fighter fired at a metal cleat beside the figure, forcing them back while workers secured a second line. Beneath a crate lid, the salvage crew found a hand-written list of names and meals for the last six days.

The barge shifted with the incoming tide. {{hero}} kept the ramp clear as a worker called out the names one by one. A reply came from inside the empty hold, where a small service hatch was bolted from the outside and the air was running low.

endings.heroWins: The crew emerged alive, and {{heroPlayer}}’s salvagers held the barge for its passengers.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took the pier and the inventory while the salvagers withdrew.
endings.draw: The passengers reached land; neither party accepted the barge’s account of its journey.

paragraphs: An underground bee farm supplied the colony’s orchards with pollinators. {{heroPlayer}}’s keepers came to retrieve a missing queen; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers had sealed the access shaft after the bees began gathering around their outdoor lights at night. Without the queen, the hives would divide before spring.

{{hero}} entered the farm with a portable lamp and followed a quiet line of workers to an empty observation chamber. There the specialist found the queen inside a cracked glass display, surrounded by a brood that had built comb against a vent. The bees were carrying pollen from flowers that grew nowhere near the colony.

The chamber fan started and drew the brood toward the vent. {{hero}} covered the display and shut the fan while the settlers opened the shaft above. The queen climbed onto the keeper’s sleeve, and the distant outdoor lights went out one after another.

endings.heroWins: The queen returned to her hive, and {{heroPlayer}}’s keepers kept the bee farm open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers closed the shaft and took charge of the threatened hives.
endings.draw: The brood survived; both groups agreed to trace the unfamiliar pollen before reopening the farm.

paragraphs: A hanging garden above the colony square was due to open for the spring festival. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers arrived to replace a cracked support; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers guarded the upper walkway because the first visitors were already climbing the stairs. Water from the garden’s irrigation trays dripped onto the crowded stalls below.

{{hero}} clipped into the maintenance rail and reached the damaged support beneath the central planter. The specialist found its bolt torn free from soft concrete, not merely loose. A child on the upper walkway dropped a festival ribbon over the edge and leaned after it as the entire garden shifted.

The rigger caught the ribbon and called for the walkway to clear. {{hero}} braced the planter with a spare strut while two workers led the visitors back down. Beneath the square, the stalls went quiet as the dripping stopped and everyone looked up at the load hanging over them.

endings.heroWins: The garden stayed aloft, and {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers held its walkway until the new supports set.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took the garden under their own watch while the riggers withdrew.
endings.draw: The festival moved to the square below; both crews kept the upper walkway closed for repairs.

paragraphs: A colony museum displayed a meteor fragment on loan from a private collector. When its return date arrived, {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors found two valid receipts for the same stone; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the gallery until the schoolchildren finished their visit. The fragment had grown heavier since its last inspection.

{{hero}} checked the display scale and discovered a second object inside the plinth. The specialist removed a maintenance panel to reveal a small locked box, its seal matching neither receipt. A teacher said the children had heard tapping from the display during the night tour, though no one had touched it.

The gallery alarm began to sound as {{hero}} reached for the box. The collector’s courier arrived at the entrance, asking for the meteor alone. The children gathered behind the teacher while the auditors moved the plinth clear of the exit, leaving the box where both groups could see it.

endings.heroWins: The auditors secured both objects, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the gallery open for an honest inventory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the museum while the courier took the fragment away.
endings.draw: The fragment stayed on display; neither side opened the unlisted box before the children left.

paragraphs: The colony’s rain catchment filled with salt after a clear night. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey party came to test the upper cistern; {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers held the valves to protect the remaining fresh water. A pale deposit traced the shape of a door along the interior wall.

{{hero}} covered the service path as a defender tried to shut the inspection hatch. The fighter fired into the empty hinge above them, forcing the hatch open for a technician. Its lamp revealed a second deposit shaped like a handprint, this one on the dry side of the wall.

A valve wheel began to turn without an engineer beside it. {{hero}} held the path while the technician reached across the cistern to stop the flow. Below, families had lined up with water containers; the first of them called that the taps smelled of the sea.

endings.heroWins: The fresh-water line was isolated, and {{heroPlayer}}’s party kept the cistern for testing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers took the valves and excluded the survey party.
endings.draw: Both groups shared the remaining clean water while the salt deposit dried into the wall.

paragraphs: A grain silo beside the colony landing field began shedding dust just as a relief aircraft lined up to land. {{heroPlayer}}’s assault team came to secure the silo; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held its lower doors and warned that one spark could ignite the dust. The aircraft needed the grain and a safe landing strip.

{{hero}} took position behind an empty hopper and covered the silo catwalk without firing toward the suspended dust. When a figure tried to release the grain chute over the runway, the fighter fired into the steel latch outside the dust cloud, jamming the mechanism long enough for the ground crew to wave the aircraft off.

The aircraft circled while workers opened a vent on the far side. {{hero}} watched the catwalk as the dust thinned, then signaled the landing field when its lights came back into view. Inside the silo a worker shouted that the blocked chute was heating, and someone had to reach it before the plane returned.

endings.heroWins: The plane landed safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the silo while the grain was unloaded.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the silo and directed the plane to another strip.
endings.draw: The landing was canceled; both groups spent the night clearing the dangerous dust.

paragraphs: Workers clearing ground for a tram line uncovered a playground beneath the new colony, its equipment clean and its swings moving. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers came to catalog the site; {{otherPlayer}}’s builders wanted it fenced before children arrived from the nearby housing block. A painted height chart showed marks dated years in the future.

{{hero}} measured the playhouse and found its smallest door led to a full-sized room below. The specialist placed a portable camera on the floor before entering. It showed chalk drawings of the tram line as it would look after construction, including a stop the builders had not planned.

A child slipped past the fence while {{hero}} carried the camera out. One swing stopped in front of them, and the child pointed to a drawn route that ran around the playhouse instead of through it. The tram survey crew was already setting stakes across that exact path.

endings.heroWins: The builders rerouted the line, and {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers kept the playground open for study.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s builders fenced the site and continued the tram survey.
endings.draw: The child returned home; both groups paused construction until they understood the drawings.

paragraphs: A solar array above the colony’s farms stopped following the sun and turned toward an unlit patch of sky. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery team came for its central controller; {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians guarded the power feed that kept irrigation pumps running. The panels cast a single broad shadow over the fields at noon.

{{hero}} covered the array’s service corridor when a defender moved to sever the controller cable. The fighter fired into an empty support bracket, forcing the defender back and leaving the feed intact. Inside the controller, a rotating image showed a craft approaching from beyond the moon, although no telescope had reported one.

The shadow moved across the irrigation pumps as the panels turned again. {{hero}} kept the corridor clear while the recovery team copied the image and the technicians prepared a manual reset. On the screen, the approaching craft changed course at the exact moment the workers touched the switch.

endings.heroWins: The controller was secured, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the array long enough to warn the farms.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians kept the array and its power feed under their control.
endings.draw: The pumps stayed running, but both teams lost the image when the panels returned to the sun.

paragraphs: A row of fishing huts stood empty after their owners reported a strange cache beneath the jetty. {{heroPlayer}}’s coastal team came to inspect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists kept the huts sealed until the families returned. The cache was arranged like a nest around a boat bell whose clapper had been removed.

{{hero}} reached beneath the wet boards with a sampler and found thin shells packed around the bell. The specialist lifted one into a clear case while the tide rose against the jetty supports. A faint clicking answered from the shells left behind, repeating the rhythm of a bell nobody had struck.

The first shell opened in the case. {{hero}} closed its vent and called the team back from the jetty, where a fisher had returned to claim the bell. The colonists watched the water climb, and the fisher said the bell had been taken from a boat lost before any of the huts were built.

endings.heroWins: The team removed the sealed sample, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people kept the jetty closed until the families were safe.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s colonists retained the jetty while the team withdrew with its case.
endings.draw: The families returned to shore; neither group disturbed the remaining shells at high tide.

paragraphs: Migrating birds began striking the colony’s new communication tower after its nighttime guidance lights changed color. {{heroPlayer}}’s systems crew came to correct the pattern; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers protected the tower because their emergency channel relied on it. At sunrise the tower base was crowded with injured birds.

{{hero}} opened the controller and found its lighting schedule copied from a tower on another planet, where birds followed a different coast. The specialist restored the local pattern while volunteers carried the injured animals to a shelter. A storm alert arrived on the emergency channel just as the lights blinked out.

The controller would accept only one active schedule. {{hero}} held a temporary bridge in place so the storm warning could transmit while the new lights came online. Above, the flock wheeled once around the tower and then settled toward the marsh, leaving the volunteers room to reach the last injured bird.

endings.heroWins: The warning went through, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the tower safe for the migrating flock.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took the controller while the systems crew left its repair incomplete.
endings.draw: The birds passed without another strike; both groups kept a watch on the emergency channel.

paragraphs: A depot of retired care machines was due to be recycled when one unit began delivering food to an address erased from the colony map. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts came to recover its route memory; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the depot locked until they knew who might still need the food.

{{hero}} followed the machine through a side service gate and found it stopping at an empty lot. The specialist checked its records: it had delivered there every morning for twelve years. Beneath the grass stood a cellar door, covered by soil but warm to the touch when the machine placed a meal above it.

The cellar door opened a finger’s width. {{hero}} held the care machine steady while the settlers cleared the soil, and someone below asked why breakfast had arrived late. In the depot behind them, other retired units powered on and began calculating routes to addresses no longer shown on any public map.

endings.heroWins: The hidden residents were reached, and {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts kept the depot open for the machines to finish their rounds.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took custody of the depot and its undisclosed routes.
endings.draw: The residents received food; both groups agreed not to erase the old routes again.

paragraphs: A bridge over the colony gorge had been chosen for a peace ceremony, but a storm knocked away its central deck before the delegates arrived. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to hold the remaining span; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers guarded the opposite bank. Both parties carried halves of the same banner.

{{hero}} crossed the narrow side rail with a safety line and met a defender at the broken deck. There was no room for a shot over the drop. The fighter forced a passage at arm’s length, then used the line to draw the loose planks toward the gap without dislodging the other half of the banner.

The delegates appeared at both ends of the bridge as rain began to fall. {{hero}} held the rail while builders secured the first plank, leaving enough room for one person at a time. A child on the far bank lifted their half of the banner and asked who would cross first.

endings.heroWins: The banner joined across the repaired span, and {{heroPlayer}}’s escort kept the bridge safe for the delegates.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the crossing while the escort withdrew from the storm.
endings.draw: The delegates met halfway, but neither side claimed the bridge when the rain returned.

paragraphs: A colonial tribunal convened in a schoolhouse to decide whether a spring belonged to the settlement or to a passing relief convoy. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators brought a witness from the convoy; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the hall and the well key. The first witness testimony had been recorded before either side arrived.

{{hero}} inspected the recorder and found its clock set a day ahead. The specialist played the testimony for everyone present: a child described finding a second spring beneath the schoolhouse, where a loose floorboard now moved with each footstep. The child in the recording stood outside the hall, listening without recognizing their own voice.

The hearing paused as {{hero}} lifted the floorboard. Fresh water shone far below a stone stair, and the well key would not fit its gate. Both parties gathered around the opening, waiting for the child to say whether they had ever been down those steps.

endings.heroWins: The tribunal heard the child, and {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators kept the new spring open to both parties.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers retained the schoolhouse and its water access.
endings.draw: The hearing adjourned with both springs protected until the stair could be surveyed.

paragraphs: A damaged lander touched down beside the colony’s cattle pasture, carrying an empty rescue capsule that continued to report a heartbeat. {{heroPlayer}}’s flight crew came to inspect its systems; {{otherPlayer}}’s ranchers held the pasture gate while children watched from behind it. The lander’s engines were too hot to approach from the front.

{{hero}} entered through a cooled service panel and followed the heartbeat signal to a cargo container strapped beneath the capsule. The specialist cut away its webbing and found a second, much older distress beacon whose battery should have died years ago. It had been transmitting the heartbeat whenever the capsule passed over the pasture.

A rancher called that one animal had wandered beneath the hot wing. {{hero}} carried the beacon outside and used its signal to guide the flight crew around the engine wash. The animal emerged unharmed, but the beacon’s pulse quickened each time it faced the farmhouse beyond the gate.

endings.heroWins: The lander was secured, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the beacon for a careful examination.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s ranchers retained the pasture and asked the flight crew to remove the lander.
endings.draw: The animals returned to the field; both crews left the beacon sealed beside the empty capsule.

paragraphs: The colony’s northern gate lost power while a night transport waited outside in falling sleet. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol came to keep the road open; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the gatehouse until the transport’s manifest could be checked. Its headlights showed people walking alongside it, carrying no luggage.

{{hero}} covered the gate from an earthwork as a figure moved to drop the road barrier onto the waiting passengers. The fighter fired at its unoccupied hinge and stopped the barrier halfway down. A woman from the transport slipped under it and handed the gatekeeper a manifest with one line rubbed through.

The patrol found the erased name stamped on an identification card beside the road. {{hero}} kept the barrier open while the passengers counted one another, each looking for the person who had walked beside them. Beyond the headlights, the sleet thickened enough to hide the transport’s far door.

endings.heroWins: The transport entered safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol held the gate until everyone was accounted for.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the barrier lowered while the patrol escorted the transport elsewhere.
endings.draw: The passengers reached shelter; the missing name remained unreadable on the manifest.

paragraphs: A kite festival had been planned on a colony ridge where the winter winds first returned. {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors brought a ceremonial kite made for an elder who could no longer climb; {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors held the ridge while a communications mast was repaired. Children waited below with their own small kites.

{{hero}} met a defender near the mast’s anchor line as the ceremonial kite lifted unexpectedly. The fighter closed to arm’s length and held the narrow path without cutting the windward cable. A fallen tool struck the kite’s string, dragging it toward the exposed mast wires.

The elder’s granddaughter caught the trailing string and called for help. {{hero}} held the defender away from the wires while she pulled the kite across the safe side of the ridge. From below, the children launched their kites one by one, filling the air with lines neither crew could cross carelessly.

endings.heroWins: The ceremonial kite reached the elder, and {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors kept the ridge for the festival.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors secured the mast and moved the festival down the slope.
endings.draw: The kites flew together while both crews left the narrow ridge path open.

paragraphs: A community bus broke down beside a colony nursery with a sealed parcel beneath its last seat. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers came to retrieve it; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers needed the bus to carry children home before nightfall. No one aboard remembered loading the parcel, although its label named the nursery.

{{hero}} opened the service panel and found the parcel wedged against the bus battery. The specialist freed it without cutting power, then read the delivery note: a packet of saplings meant for a field the colony had abandoned after the soil turned gray. The oldest child said they had seen green shoots there that morning.

The bus engine caught on its final attempt. {{hero}} carried the packet to the nursery gate while the settlers counted the children. The courier could keep the parcel for its recorded recipient or send the bus toward the abandoned field, whose road would be difficult after dark.

endings.heroWins: The saplings reached their field, and {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers kept the nursery route open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the bus and parcel at the nursery for the night.
endings.draw: The children reached home; both groups agreed to inspect the field at first light.

paragraphs: A deer crossing ran directly through the colony’s unfinished junction. {{heroPlayer}}’s road patrol came to keep its temporary barriers open; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers had prepared to pour concrete before the morning traffic. A line of deer stood among the traffic signs, refusing to turn back.

{{hero}} covered the junction from a retaining wall when a vehicle accelerated toward the crossing. The fighter fired into an empty road marker beside the driver, making them brake before the herd. The deer moved past the stopped vehicle, but a fawn remained trapped between two temporary steel fences.

The concrete mixer arrived behind the vehicle. {{hero}} held the roadway clear as a settler loosened the fence bolts and guided the fawn out. Beyond the junction, the herd waited at the tree line instead of disappearing, as if it would not continue without its last member.

endings.heroWins: The fawn rejoined the herd, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol kept the crossing open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers controlled the junction and redirected the herd around the new road.
endings.draw: The deer passed; both groups delayed the concrete until a safe crossing could be marked.

paragraphs: A pond outside the colony began flowering under its surface, drawing families to watch the lights beneath the water. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers came to collect a sample; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers guarded the bank because the pond supplied their irrigation canal. A week earlier, the water had been clear enough to see the bottom.

{{hero}} lowered a transparent tube and caught a single glowing filament. The specialist watched it divide when exposed to sunlight and stop when the tube entered shade. Beneath the bank, an old drain fed water from a second pond the settlers believed had dried up years ago.

The irrigation pump turned on, pulling the flowers toward its intake. {{hero}} shaded the sampling tube and worked with the settlers to close the pump for a few minutes. Along the old drain, the first flowers appeared in the supposedly dry pond, far beyond where their lights could be seen.

endings.heroWins: The sample survived, and {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers kept the pond safe while its waters were traced.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the irrigation bank and barred further sampling.
endings.draw: The canal stayed clear; both parties watched the second pond flower after sunset.

paragraphs: A paymaster disappeared before a construction crew could collect the wages owed for the colony’s floodwall. {{heroPlayer}}’s contracted guards tracked the payroll case to a shuttered bakery; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the street to prevent anyone from carrying the colony funds away. The ovens were warm although the bakery had been closed all week.

{{hero}} covered the rear exit when a figure with the case moved through the kitchen. The fighter fired at the empty metal rack beside the door, forcing the figure to leave the case behind. Its lock had been opened already, and the payroll envelopes inside bore the workers’ names in correct order.

The bakers returned as the construction crew gathered outside. {{hero}} held the rear yard clear while a foreman counted the envelopes under the bakery lamps. One was missing. On a flour-covered counter lay its contents and a note asking that the money go to a worker injured on the wall.

endings.heroWins: The crew received its wages, and {{heroPlayer}}’s guards kept the case until the missing worker was found.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took custody of the case and paid the crew themselves.
endings.draw: The wages were distributed; both groups searched for the injured worker before leaving.

paragraphs: A rail depot received a night train with its doors locked and a child’s bicycle tied to the last car. {{heroPlayer}}’s security team came to inspect the cargo; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the platform for passengers expected on the next train. Someone inside the locked car rang its service bell once.

{{hero}} covered the end of the platform while a worker cut the cargo seal. A figure at the far signal box raised a weapon, and the fighter fired at a track lamp to turn them from the car. The worker opened the door onto rows of empty seats and a bicycle helmet on the floor.

A second bell rang beneath the carriage. {{hero}} kept the signal box in sight as workers crawled under the frame and found a cramped luggage space with a person inside. The next train sounded from beyond the bend, giving the team minutes to clear the platform.

endings.heroWins: The hidden passenger reached safety, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the depot ready for the next train.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took control of the platform as the security team withdrew.
endings.draw: Both groups helped the passenger out; the bicycle’s owner never came forward.

paragraphs: The colony’s tool shed held equipment needed to rebuild a collapsed storm barrier. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired crew arrived for the cutting gear; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers had locked the shed after noticing several tools marked with names of workers still missing beyond the barrier. Rain was gathering over the lower houses.

{{hero}} covered the lane while a technician checked the shed lock. A figure on the opposite roof tried to draw the crew away; the fighter fired at an empty gutter and kept them back without striking the families sheltering below. Inside the shed, the technician found a cutting torch with a freshly emptied fuel tank.
